What Is This Short List For?

Candidates often ask what the purpose of this short list is. In short, it identifies who will be called next for physical and practical testing before the final ranked list is prepared.

The register numbers published are provisionally shortlisted to appear for the Physical Measurement and Practical Test, which includes a T-Test and a Road Test. This is a screening stage, not the final selection. Inclusion in the short list does not guarantee a place in the eventual Ranked List; it only confirms eligibility to proceed to the next stage, subject to document verification.

The 74 candidates in the Result List secured the top marks in the OMR examination. The lowest qualifying mark in the Result List is 29.6700. The Supplementary List was prepared separately to ensure adequate representation of candidates from reserved categories (SC, ST, OBC, and EWS) as required under reservation rules, drawing candidates from lower mark ranges within their respective categories.

Important Instructions for Shortlisted Candidates

This section outlines the key requirements and conditions every shortlisted candidate must be aware of before appearing for the Physical Measurement and Practical Test.

  • Provisional status: Inclusion in the short list is purely provisional and subject to scrutiny and verification of the application on an absolute basis. It does not confer any right to inclusion in the final Ranked List.
  • No late claims: The short list is based solely on details furnished in the original application. Subsequent claims will not be entertained at any stage.
  • Personal appearance required: Shortlisted candidates must appear in person with original documents for the Physical Measurement and Practical Test (T-Test and Road Test). The date, time, and venue will be communicated via Profile Message and SMS.
  • Valid driving license mandatory: Candidates must hold a valid Driving License with endorsement for Heavy Goods Vehicle (HGV) and Heavy Passenger Vehicle (HPV) with badge, throughout all stages of selection - from the last date of application submission to the date of OTR (Original documents verification) of the Ranked List.
  • Category certificates: OBC candidates must produce a Non-Creamy Layer Certificate as per G.O. (P) No.81/2009/SCSTDD dated 26.09.2009. SC/ST candidates must produce a Community Certificate (Form III or digitally signed) issued by a Revenue Authority not below the rank of Tahsildar. EWS candidates must produce an EWS Certificate as per G.O.(MS) No.2/2020/P&ARD dated 12.02.2020, issued by the Village Officer.
  • Revaluation policy: Revaluation of OMR answer scripts is not permitted, but rechecking is allowed after the Ranked List is published. Detailed instructions will accompany the Ranked List.
  • Answer script copies: Candidates can apply for a copy of their OMR answer script (25-02-2026 exam) by remitting the prescribed fee, after the Ranked List is approved.

Reporting Timeline

This section explains the deadline by which selected candidates must report for duty.

  • Selected employees must report to the Regional General Manager of their posted area within 30 days from the date of the office order.
  • If a selected candidate does not join within 30 days, their selection will automatically stand cancelled without any further notice, and the candidate will be solely responsible for this.

Probation Period

This section explains the probation rules applicable after joining.

  • Selected candidates will remain on probation for 6 months from the date of joining the selected post.
  • If performance during probation is not found satisfactory, the probation period may be extended, or the candidate may be reverted to their original post.

Training Period and Confirmation

This section explains the training duration before a trainee is confirmed on the post.

  • Selected candidates will undergo training for a period of 1 year from the date of joining the selected post.
  • After successful completion of training, they will be confirmed as Pharmacist in T&S Grade C.
  • Area-wise posting of selected candidates within the region will be decided by the concerned Regional General Manager.

How to Check RRB Group D Result 2026

This section walks candidates through the exact steps to access and download their individual result and scorecard from the official RRB portal.

Candidates can follow these steps to check their RRB Group D Result 2026:

  1. Visit the official website of the RRB region under which you applied.

RRB Group D Zone-Wise Result: What It Contains

Since RRB Group D results are declared separately by each regional board, this section explains how the zone-wise system works and what candidates will find in their result PDF.

The RRB Group D Result 2026 is published individually by each of the 21 RRB zones on their respective regional websites, rather than through a single centralized portal. Candidates need to log in with their user ID and password to download it; RRB does not send a physical copy by post.

Candidates who qualify in the CBT will proceed through the following stages:

  • Physical Efficiency Test (PET): A qualifying-only round involving physical tasks; separate standards apply for male and female candidates.

  • It is very easy to download Delhi DSSSB Admit Card / Call Letter.

  • First Method: In this method, you will have to enter your date of birth along with class 10 roll number, passing year and your password, after that you can directly download the admit card from the dashboard.

The Central Bank of India Apprentice Exam 2026 is scheduled for 5th July 2026 (Sunday) and will be conducted by BFSI SSC in online computer-based test mode. This article explains the admit card release details, exam date, download steps, eligibility, exam pattern, and everything else candidates need before exam day.

CBI Apprentice 2026 Important Dates

  • Notification Released: 12 June 2026
  • Online Application Start Date: 12 June 2026
  • Online Application Last Date: 28 June 2026 (extended)
  • Admit Card Release Date: 2 July 2026
  • Online Exam Date: 5 July 2026 (Sunday)

Candidates should keep checking the official website for updates regarding the Local Language Proficiency Test schedule, which is typically announced after the online exam result.

CBI Apprentice Vacancy Details 2026

The Central Bank of India has announced a total of 4,500 Apprentice vacancies for the financial year 2026-27, distributed across various states and union territories. Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh reportedly have the largest state-wise allocations. Candidates are advised to refer to the official notification PDF on the bank's recruitment page for the exact state-wise and category-wise vacancy breakup, since detailed figures for every state were not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Category Age Relaxation
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
SC / ST 5 years
PwBD (UR/EWS) 10 years
PwBD (OBC) 13 years
PwBD (SC/ST) 15 years

Candidates should check the official notification for the exact category-wise age relaxation applicable to them.

Salary / Stipend Details

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. This is a training stipend rather than a regular salary, and no other allowances or benefits are provided. Completion of the apprenticeship does not guarantee permanent employment with the bank.

Application Fee

The exact application fee amount for the CBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article. Candidates should refer to the official Central Bank of India Apprentice notification PDF on centralbank.bank.in for accurate, category-wise fee details, since this cannot be reliably stated here.

Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

Documents Required at the Exam Centre

  • Printed copy of the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original government-issued photo ID proof, such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence
  • A photocopy of the photo ID for verification
  • Recent passport-size photographs, as specified in the admit card instructions

Candidates should ensure the name on their ID proof matches the name printed on the admit card to avoid denial of entry.

How to Download the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026

Follow these steps to download your Central Bank of India Apprentice hall ticket:

  1. Visit the official website of the Central Bank of India at centralbankofindia.co.in or centralbank.bank.in.
  2. Go to the "Recruitment" or "Careers" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the "CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026" or "Download Call Letter" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password or Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code, if required.
  6. Click the Login or Submit button.
  7. Your CBI Apprentice Hall Ticket 2026 will appear on the screen.
  8. Carefully verify all details, including your name, photograph, signature, exam date, and exam centre.
  9. Download the admit card and take a clear printout on an A4 sheet for the examination.

Central Bank of India Apprentice Exam Pattern 2026

The online written examination consists of 100 objective-type questions worth 100 marks, to be completed in 60 minutes, with no negative marking.

Subject Questions Marks Medium
General/Financial Awareness 20 20 English/Hindi
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 20 20 English/Hindi
Computer Knowledge 20 20 English/Hindi
General English 20 20 English
Central Bank of India Products & Services 20 20 English
Total 100 100 -

Important Instructions for Exam Day

  • Reach the exam centre well before the reporting time mentioned on your individual admit card.
  • Carry the printed admit card; digital copies on a phone or tablet are typically not accepted.
  • Do not carry prohibited items such as mobile phones, smartwatches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, bags, or study material into the exam hall.
  • Check your name, photograph, exam centre address, and category details on the admit card, and report any discrepancy to the helpdesk immediately.
  • Wear simple clothing and avoid accessories like jewellery or metal items, as per standard exam-day dress code guidelines followed by the bank.

The Phase 1 exam is qualifying in nature only scores from this stage are used solely to shortlist candidates for Phase 2 (Mains). Marks from Phase 1 do not contribute to the final merit list.

RBI Grade B Mains Admit Card 2026 - Expected in July

With Phase 1 completed, all attention now turns to the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Admit Card 2026, which is expected to be released in July 2026, ahead of the Mains exam scheduled on 25th July 2026 for General posts and 26th July 2026 for DEPR/DSIM posts. RBI typically releases the Mains hall ticket approximately 7 to 10 days before the exam date, so candidates should watch the official website closely during the second week of July.

The Mains exam is a comprehensive paper that tests a candidate's knowledge of Economic and Social Issues, Finance and Management, and English Writing Skills. Unlike Phase 1, Phase 2 marks are directly counted in the final selection.

 

How to Download RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026

Downloading the RBI Grade B call letter is a straightforward process. The same steps apply for both Phase 1 (already released) and Phase 2 (upcoming). Follow the steps below to access your hall ticket from the official website.

Step 1: Visit the official RBI recruitment portal at https://opportunities.rbi.org.in/

Step 2: Look for the admit card link under the "Call Letter" section select the link for the relevant phase (Phase 1 or Phase 2).

Step 3: A login page will appear on your screen.

Step 4: Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth / Password in the respective fields.

Step 5: Click on the Submit button. Your RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 will be displayed on the screen.

Step 6: Carefully verify all the details printed on the call letter name, roll number, exam centre, and shift timing.

Step 7: Download and take at least 2 printouts to carry on exam day.

Step 8: Read all exam day instructions mentioned on the call letter before the examination.

Details to Verify on Your RBI Grade B Call Letter

After downloading the admit card, candidates must cross-check the following details to ensure everything is accurate. If any discrepancy is found, it must be reported to RBI's recruitment authorities immediately.

The call letter will contain the following information:

Candidate's Name, Roll Number and Registration Number, Photograph and Signature, Date of Birth, Category (UR/OBC/SC/ST/EWS/PwBD), Post Applied For, Exam Date and Shift Timing, Reporting Time and Gate Closing Time, Exam Centre Name, Address, and Code, and Important Exam Day Instructions.

Documents to Carry to the RBI Grade B Exam Centre

Carrying the right documents to the examination centre is mandatory. Entry will not be granted if the candidate fails to produce valid identity proof along with the printed admit card.

Every candidate must bring the following on exam day:

Printed copy of the RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026, 2 recent passport-size photographs, one valid original Photo ID proof such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence, and a photocopy of the same Photo ID.

PwBD candidates should additionally refer to the Instructions for PwBD Candidates using Scribe and/or Compensatory Time document available on the official website.

RBI Grade B Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates prepare effectively for both phases of the selection process. The RBI Grade B selection consists of Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and an Interview round.

Phase 1 Exam Pattern - Objective Type (Qualifying)

Phase 1 is a 2-hour online objective exam carrying 200 marks across 200 questions. Since it is only qualifying, candidates must clear it to advance to Mains, but these marks do not count toward the final score.

Section Questions Marks Duration
Reasoning Ability 60 60 45 Minutes
English Language 30 30 25 Minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 30 25 Minutes
General Knowledge (GA) 80 80 25 Minutes
Total 200 200 120 Minutes

Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Pattern - Objective + Descriptive

Phase 2 is the main scoring round with 300 marks spread across 3 papers. Both objective and descriptive components are tested. Marks from this stage directly determine the final merit list.

Paper Subject Question Type Marks Duration
Paper I Economic & Social Issues (ESI) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Paper II English (Writing Skills) Descriptive 100 90 Minutes
Paper III Finance & Management (FM) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Total     300 330 Minutes

RBI Grade B Exam Day Instructions 2026

RBI has issued specific instructions that every candidate must follow on exam day. Non-compliance may result in disqualification from the examination.

Candidates must reach the exam centre before the gate closing time without fail. Biometric verification including thumb impression and photograph capture will be conducted at the centre. Ensure your name on the admit card matches exactly with your photo ID. Wearing clothes with metal items, large buttons, or accessories that could trigger security checks should be avoided. The IBPS PO/MT-XVI Selection Process 2026 consists of four stages: Online Preliminary Examination, Online Main Examination, Personality Test, and Common Interview. Step 3: Personality Test

Candidates who qualify the Main Examination are called for a self-report Personality Test, which is non-qualifying in nature but mandatory to attend for interview eligibility. The Personality Test may be conducted in proctored mode or at designated examination centres, as decided by IBPS.

Step 4: Common Interview

The interview carries 100 marks, with minimum qualifying marks of 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates). The final combined score is calculated using a weightage ratio of 80:20 between the Main Examination and Interview respectively.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for IBPS PO/MT-XVI 2026

Many candidates unintentionally get their applications rejected due to avoidable errors during the online registration process. Being aware of these common pitfalls in advance can help candidates complete their IBPS PO/MT-XVI application smoothly.

  • Uploading a signature or handwritten declaration in capital letters, which is not accepted under any circumstances.
  • Entering the 'Name', 'Email ID', 'Mobile Number', or 'Nationality' fields incorrectly, since these cannot be edited after submission.
  • Waiting until the last date to pay fees, which risks failure due to heavy website traffic near the deadline.
  • Uploading blurred or smudged photographs, signatures, or thumb impressions that don't meet the prescribed file size and dimension limits.
  • Selecting the wrong category and later expecting it to be changed after the Edit Window closes.
  • Forgetting to retain multiple copies of the uploaded photograph, which is required at several later stages of the process.
  • Not indicating scribe requirements or compensatory time preferences at the time of registration, since such requests are not entertained later.

RRB Technician Eligibility Criteria 2026

Anyone wondering who can apply for RRB Technician 2026 should know that eligibility depends on educational qualification, age limit, and medical standards specific to each post. The qualification requirements vary by department, and candidates must satisfy these conditions on or before the closing date, 29 July 2026, since those awaiting final results are not eligible to apply.

Educational Qualification

For Technician Grade-I Signal, candidates need a Bachelor of Science in Physics/Electronics/Computer Science/Information Technology/Instrumentation, a three-year diploma in Engineering, or a Degree in Engineering in these streams. For most Technician Grade-III posts, candidates need Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT or Matriculation/SSLC plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in the relevant trade (such as Fitter, Welder, Electrician, Machinist, Carpenter, or Blacksmith, depending on the post applied for).

Age Limit (as on 01 July 2026)

Technician Grade-III 18 years 30 years

Age Relaxation

Candidates from reserved categories get standard relaxation in the upper age limit: 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC-NCL, and additional relaxation for PwBD candidates (10 years for UR/EWS, 13 years for OBC-NCL, 15 years for SC/ST). Ex-servicemen get age relaxation equal to their length of service plus 3 years (UR/EWS), 6 years (OBC-NCL), or 8 years (SC/ST) after deducting service length from their actual age.

RRB Technician Application Fee 2026

The application fee for RRB Technician CEN 02/2026 differs by candidate category and is partially refundable for those who appear in the CBT. General category candidates pay more than reserved categories, with both fee structures eligible for partial refund upon attending the exam.

RRB Technician Selection Process 2026

Candidates often ask how RRB selects Technicians, and the answer is a three-stage process based purely on merit. The recruitment involves a Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification (DV), and a Medical Examination, with shortlisting at each stage determined by performance in the previous one.

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT): A single CBT of 90 minutes with 100 questions and negative marking of 1/3rd mark per wrong answer. Minimum qualifying marks are 40% (UR/EWS), 30% (OBC-NCL/SC), and 25% (ST).
  2. Document Verification (DV): Candidates are shortlisted at a 1:1 ratio against vacancies based on CBT merit, RRB-wise. Original documents must be produced; no extra time is given for missing certificates.
  3. Medical Examination (ME): Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities as per the medical standard (A3, B1, B2, or C1) prescribed for the specific post.

Based on typical RRB recruitment cycles, CBT is expected a few months after the application closes, followed by DV and medical examination in subsequent phases - though exact dates will be announced on official RRB websites.

  2. Click on "Create an Account" and enter your name, father's name, mother's name, and date of birth exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
  3. Use DigiLocker or Aadhaar for identity authentication to ensure smoother verification later.
  4. Log in and fill the online application form, selecting your preferred RRB and Pay Level (5 or 2).
  5. Provide order of preference for posts under the chosen RRB and Pay Level.
  6. Capture your live photograph through webcam or mobile camera as instructed (pre-existing photos are not accepted).
  7. Upload your signature in JPG/JPEG format (30–49 KB, black ink on white paper, running handwriting).
  8. Pay the examination fee online through net banking, debit/credit card, or UPI.
  9. Submit the application and save the registration number for future reference.

Candidates shortlisted for Document Verification must carry all original certificates along with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Required documents include Matriculation/educational qualification certificates, ITI/Apprenticeship certificates, caste/category certificates (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS as applicable in the prescribed Annexure format), a valid original photo ID, and an NOC from the current employer if already employed in government service.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for RRB Technician 2026

Many candidates lose their candidature due to avoidable errors rather than ineligibility. Being aware of these common pitfalls can help applicants submit a clean, error-free application the first time.

  • Entering wrong name/DOB: Details in "Create an Account" cannot be changed later - always match them exactly with your Matriculation certificate.
  • Applying to multiple RRBs for the same Pay Level: This leads to rejection of all applications and debarment from future RRB/RRC exams.
  • Uploading a pre-existing or printed photo: Only live-captured photographs are accepted; printed photo uploads cause summary rejection.
  • Signature in capital/block letters: Signatures must be in cursive running handwriting with black ink - block letters are grounds for rejection.
  • Missing the fee payment deadline: Fee must be paid by 31 July 2026, two days after the application deadline - don't assume submission alone is enough.
  • Ignoring the modification window: Errors (other than account details and chosen RRB) can be corrected only between 1–10 August 2026 by paying ₹250 per modification.

Application Fee – IOCL Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The IOCL Apprentice Recruitment 2026 notification does not mention any application fee for any category. Candidates can apply online through the NAPS/NATS portals and the Microsoft Forms link without any fee payment.

Selection Process – IndianOil Apprentice Recruitment 2026

There is no written test for the IOCL Apprentice Recruitment 2026. Selection for all four refinery units is entirely merit-based, with the merit list prepared on the basis of aggregate percentage of marks in the prescribed qualifying examination. Candidates applying for apprenticeship training for the first time will be given preference over those applying for a second time.

  1. Merit List Preparation: Candidates are ranked in descending order of percentage of marks in the prescribed qualification (aggregate of all years/semesters).
  2. Tie-breaking: In case of a tie in percentage, the candidate senior by age (earlier date of birth) is ranked higher. If date of birth is also the same, the candidate with a higher percentage in Matriculation is ranked higher.
  3. Shortlisting for Document Verification: Candidates are shortlisted based on merit and available seats. Tentative date of publication of shortlist is 05 August 2026.
  4. Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must appear in person with original documents. Tentatively scheduled from 11 August 2026 to 18 August 2026.
  5. Pre-Engagement Medical Examination: Candidates must pass a medical fitness test as prescribed under the Apprentices Act. Only candidates declared medically fit will proceed.
  6. Offer of Engagement: Candidates whose documents and medical fitness are found in order will receive a formal engagement offer.

IOCL Apprentice Stipend / Salary 2026

The stipend for IOCL Apprentice 2026 will be paid as prescribed under the Apprentices Act, 1961/1973 and Apprentices Rules 1992 (as amended) along with Corporation's guidelines. The official notification does not mention a specific monthly stipend amount. Apprentices will not receive HRA or Company accommodation. They will, however, receive accident insurance coverage and safety equipment (safety shoes and helmet) for selected trades.

How to Apply for IOCL Apprentice Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online

The application process for the IndianOil Apprentice Recruitment 2026 is a mandatory two-step online process. Both Step I (NAPS/NATS portal registration and application) and Step II (Microsoft Forms submission) must be completed; completing only one step will result in an invalid application. The application window is open from 29 June 2026 (10:00 hrs) to 28 July 2026 (17:00 hrs) at www.iocl.com.

Step I – Register and Apply on NAPS or NATS Portal

For Codes 101, 102, 103, 108, 109, 110, and 111: Register on the NAPS portal at https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in/ and apply for the relevant IOCL refinery opportunity using the establishment ID for NAPS provided above.

For Codes 104, 105, 106, and 107: Register on the NATS portal at https://nats.education.gov.in and apply for the advertisement notified by the specific IOCL refinery unit on your dashboard using the establishment ID for NATS provided above.

  3. Read the detailed advertisement carefully.
  4. Ensure your profile is registered and 100% correctly updated on the relevant NAPS or NATS portal.
  5. Log in to the NAPS/NATS portal using your User ID/Email ID and apply for the apprenticeship opportunity under the applicable refinery's Establishment ID.
  6. After successfully applying on NAPS/NATS, go back to www.iocl.com and click on the Microsoft Forms link for your refinery unit.

Common Mistakes to Avoid in IOCL Apprentice Apply Online 2026

Many candidates make easily avoidable errors while applying for the IOCL Apprentice Vacancy 2026 that result in summary rejection. The following points are based on common patterns in similar PSU apprenticeship recruitment drives and are not derived from the official notification.

  1. Completing only Step I or only Step II: Both NAPS/NATS portal application and Microsoft Forms submission are mandatory. Completing only one will make the application invalid.
  2. Mismatched details across Step I and Step II: The Enrolment No., email ID, and mobile number used in NAPS/NATS must exactly match those submitted in the Microsoft Forms. Any mismatch leads to rejection.
  3. Applying for more than one trade/discipline: The notification explicitly states that candidates applying for more than one trade/discipline will be summarily rejected.
  4. Applying with qualifications acquired through distance/correspondence/part-time mode: Only regular full-time courses are eligible. Distance education qualifications are not accepted.
  5. Candidates with higher qualifications (BE/B.Tech/MBA/CA etc.) applying: Those possessing or having completed higher professional qualifications before joining are not eligible and will be rejected at document verification.
  6. Not converting CGPA to percentage before applying: Candidates with CGPA/Grade-based marksheets must mention the equivalent percentage as per their institute's norms and carry a conversion certificate to document verification.
  7. Waiting until the last minute: The portal closes at 17:00 hrs on 28 July 2026. Technical issues near the deadline are common - apply well in advance.
  8. Not updating NAPS/NATS profile to 100%: Incomplete profiles may cause the application to be treated as invalid. Always verify the profile before applying.

MPESB Agriculture Extension Officer Eligibility Criteria 2026

Educational Qualification

The educational qualification for MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Recruitment 2026 is a Graduate degree (Bachelor's degree) in Agriculture or Horticulture from a recognised university.

  • The qualification must be fully completed on or before the date of submitting the online application. Candidates acquiring the degree after the application date will not be considered eligible.
  • The marksheet number, marks obtained and maximum marks of the qualifying degree must be entered in the online form.

Age Limit (As on 1 January 2026)

The minimum age for all candidates is 18 years. The maximum age limit is calculated as on 1 January 2026 and varies by category as shown below.

Category Maximum Age
Unreserved (Open direct recruitment) 40 years
MP domicile SC / ST / OBC candidates 45 years
Women candidates of MP (reserved and unreserved) 45 years
MP Government / Corporation / Board employees, Home Guards, Divyangjan (PwD) 45 years
EWS candidates 40 years (no age relaxation for EWS)
Contract (Samvida) employees and Rule-14 priority categories Up to 55 years (as per applicable relaxation rules)

Other Eligibility Conditions

  • The candidate must be a citizen of India (Nepal citizens may be eligible subject to the certificate required under MP Civil Services Recruitment Rules, 1961).
  • Live registration in an Employment Office of Madhya Pradesh is mandatory for all applicants.
  • Candidates who are not domiciles of Madhya Pradesh can apply only against Unreserved (Open) posts and will not get any fee concession, reservation or age relaxation.
  • A candidate having more than two children, where one child is born on or after 26 January 2001, is not eligible for appointment.
  • Candidates who married before the legal age (18 years for women, 21 years for men) are not eligible for appointment.
  • Since the post is an Executive (Karyapalik) post, Baiga, Sahariya/Saharia and Bharia special primitive tribe candidates do not get exam exemption; they must apply online and appear in the exam as ST candidates.
  • Aadhaar registration is mandatory, and the Aadhaar must be unlocked at the time of biometric verification.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Salary 2026

Selected candidates will be appointed in the pay scale of Rs. 25,300 – 80,500 (Class III). As per the MP General Administration Department circular dated 12 December 2019, a stipend is paid during the probation period instead of the full pay scale:

  • First year: 70% of the minimum of the pay scale (approximately Rs. 17,710 per month)
  • Second year: 80% of the minimum of the pay scale (approximately Rs. 20,240 per month)
  • Third year: 90% of the minimum of the pay scale (approximately Rs. 22,770 per month)

After successful completion of the probation period, the regular pay in the scale of Rs. 25,300 – 80,500, along with admissible allowances, is paid.

Category Exam Fee

Direct Recruitment – Backlog posts No fee
  • MP Online portal fee: Rs. 60 if the form is filled through a kiosk, or Rs. 20 if filled through a registered citizen user login.
  • Correction fee: Rs. 20 per correction, plus a portal fee of Rs. 40 for each correction made during the correction window.
  • The fee can be paid through credit card, debit card, net banking or at an authorised MP Online kiosk.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Selection Process 2026

The selection for the Agriculture Extension Officer post will be made through a single online written exam followed by document verification. There is no interview.

  1. Online Written Exam (CBT): Objective-type paper of 200 marks conducted by MPESB.
  2. Normalization: If the exam is held in multiple shifts, results are prepared using the Normalised Equi-Percentile (NEP) scaling technique.
  3. Merit List and Waiting List: MPESB prepares a post-wise merit list; a waiting list of 15% of the total posts remains valid for one year or until the next exam result, whichever is earlier.
  4. Document Verification: Certificates are verified by the Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department, not by MPESB.
  5. Appointment: Appointment orders are to be issued within a maximum of three months from the date of the selection list.

Minimum Qualifying Marks

  • Unreserved (UR): 50% marks
  • SC / ST / OBC / EWS / Divyangjan: 40% marks (after 10% relaxation)

EWS candidates get the 10% relaxation in qualifying marks, but their selection is made on merit from the EWS list.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Exam Pattern 2026

The exam consists of a single question paper of 200 marks with two parts, to be solved in 3 hours.

Part Subjects Marks
Part A General Knowledge, General Hindi, General English, General Maths, General Reasoning Ability, General Science, General Computer Knowledge 100
Part B Subject-based questions (Agriculture / Horticulture) 100
Total   200
  • Questions are objective (MCQ) type with four options each, in Hindi and English medium.
  • Each correct answer carries 1 mark.
  • Negative marking applies: 0.25 marks are deducted for every wrong answer, as per clause 3.8 of the official rulebook.
  • After the exam, candidates must confirm their RAW score (number of correct answers) displayed on the computer screen before submitting.
  • Objections against questions can be filed online within three days of the objection link going live, with a fee of Rs. 150 per question.
  • There is no provision for re-evaluation or re-totalling after the result is declared.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Syllabus 2026

Part A: General Subjects (100 Marks)

  • General Knowledge
  • General Hindi
  • General English
  • General Maths
  • General Reasoning Ability
  • General Science
  • General Computer Knowledge

Part B: Agriculture Subject Syllabus (100 Marks)

  1. General Agriculture: Agriculture and its importance in the national economy.
  2. Agronomy: Major crops of MP, agro-techniques of major field crops of MP, farming systems and sustainable agriculture, introductory agro-meteorology, agro-climatic and agro-ecological zones.
  3. Soil Science: Soil composition and its role in crop production; physical, chemical and biological properties of soil; essential plant nutrients, their functions and dynamics; integrated nutrient management; problem soils and their management.
  4. Soil and Water Conservation: Watershed management.
  5. Plant Physiology: Absorption, translocation and metabolism of nutrients; photosynthesis and respiration; growth and development; growth regulators.
  6. Crop Improvement: Elements of genetics and plant breeding as applied to crop improvement.
  7. Horticulture: Package of practices for important fruits, vegetables, spices and flowering plants; nursery management and propagation methods; physiological disorders and their management; post-harvest management and value addition.
  8. Plant Protection: Important insect pests and diseases and their management; integrated pest and disease management; spray equipment selection and maintenance; rodent management; pesticide safety precautions.
  9. Agricultural Economics: Principles of economics applied to agriculture; farm planning and resource management; farming systems; marketing of agricultural produce and regulated markets in MP (including e-Chaupal); pricing of agricultural produce.
  10. Agricultural Extension Education: Philosophy, objectives and principles of extension; extension organisations at state, district and block levels; communication methods; role of farmers' organisations; role and importance of training; important rural development programmes in India.

Applicants must select four exam city preferences while filling the online form. Exam centres are allotted randomly, subject to seat availability, and MPESB's decision on centre allotment is final. The written exam is proposed to be held in the following 11 cities:

Documents Required for MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Recruitment 2026

Documents to Upload with the Online Application

  • Recent colour photograph (white background, not older than three months, with the candidate's name and date of photograph printed on it, both ears clearly visible)
  • Scanned signature (short signatures, signatures in capital letters, or multiple signatures are not accepted)
  • Handwriting sample (two lines in the candidate's own handwriting, in the prescribed format)
  • Class 8th / 10th / 12th marksheet as proof of date of birth
  • Caste / category certificate (SC / ST / OBC / EWS) issued by the competent MP authority, where applicable
  • Disability certificate for Divyangjan candidates, issued by the competent authority
  • Contract service certificate (minimum five years of continuous samvida service) for contract employee quota claimants
  • Bonus-mark certificates such as the NCC 'C' certificate, where applicable

Documents to Carry on Exam Day

  • Admit card (Test Admit Card – TAC) downloaded from esb.mp.gov.in, with Part 2 entries duly filled
  • Original photo ID: Voter ID, PAN Card, Aadhaar Card, Driving Licence or Passport (an e-Aadhaar printout is valid only if verified by UIDAI)
  • Black ballpoint pen

How to Apply for MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Recruitment 2026

Only online applications are accepted; offline applications will be rejected. Follow these steps to apply between 3 July and 17 July 2026:

  1. Visit the official MPESB website esb.mp.gov.in or the MP Online portal mponline.gov.in.
  2. Open the application link for "Group-2 Sub Group-1 Krishi Vistar Adhikari Recruitment Test 2026".
  3. Read the rulebook and eligibility conditions carefully before starting the form.
  4. Fill in personal details, Aadhaar number/VID, permanent body identification marks, photo ID details, and educational qualification details (marksheet number, marks obtained and maximum marks).
  5. Upload the photograph, signature and handwriting sample in the prescribed JPG format.
  6. Select four exam city preferences in order of priority.
  7. Pay the application fee through credit card, debit card, net banking or an authorised MP Online kiosk.
  8. Submit the form, note down the application number, and keep a printout of the application and fee receipt safely. The application number is required to download the admit card.

Important Instructions for Applicants

  • Aadhaar registration is compulsory, and multi-level Aadhaar-enabled biometric verification will be done at the exam centre. Keep your Aadhaar biometrics unlocked on the exam day; otherwise, entry to the exam will be denied.
  • Entry to the exam centre is allowed only up to the reporting time. Latecomers will not be admitted.
  • Mobile phones, calculators, log tables, digital watches, sunglasses, whitener, and all electronic devices are strictly prohibited inside the exam hall. Violations are treated as Unfair Means (UFM) cases.
  • Candidates cannot leave the exam hall before the exam ends.
  • The educational qualification must be complete on or before the date of applying; final-year or result-awaited candidates are not eligible.
  • Eligibility in the online exam is purely provisional; certificates are verified by the department during the appointment process.
  • Any wrong information or impersonation leads to cancellation of candidature, and impersonation cases also invite an FIR and legal action.
  • No correction of any kind is allowed after the correction window closes on 22 July 2026, and no correction is entertained after the admit card is issued.
  • Objections to questions can be submitted only online, within three days of the objection link opening, at Rs. 150 per question.
  • Travel expense reimbursement (for eligible MP domicile SC / ST / OBC and PwD candidates) is paid by the department through e-payment; submit bank details in Proforma-1 with the required enclosures.
  • For application-related help, contact the MP Online helpdesk at 0755-6720200 or the MPESB toll-free number 18002337899. Complaints can be emailed to [email protected].

HPCL Officer Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Candidates preparing for the HPCL Junior Executive and Officer Recruitment 2026 should understand that selection involves multiple stages depending on the post applied for. The process combines a Computer Based Test with further shortlisting rounds.

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT): Consists of General Aptitude (English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, Logical Reasoning & Data Interpretation) and Technical/Professional Knowledge related to the qualifying degree. Tentatively scheduled for August/September 2026.
  2. Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must upload/submit supporting documents as per merit and category-wise ratio.
  3. Group Task and/or Personal Interview: Conducted for candidates who clear the CBT and document scrutiny stage.
  4. Psychometric Assessment: May be conducted before or after the Group Task/Personal Interview.
  5. Physical Fitness Efficiency Test (PFET): Applicable where required - includes Working at Height Test, Endurance Test, and Agility Test, conducted after the medical exam.
  6. Pre-Employment Medical Examination (PEME): Conducted in HPCL nominated/empanelled hospitals; there is no provision for re-examination or appeal.

Candidates must secure minimum qualifying marks at each applicable stage to remain in contention. A category and discipline-wise merit list is then prepared based on combined performance across all stages.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates face avoidable issues while applying for government and PSU recruitment drives. Keeping the following points in mind can help ensure a smooth HPCL Recruitment 2026 application process.

  • Do not wait until the last day (20 July 2026) to submit your application, as heavy website traffic can cause payment or submission failures.
  • Double-check your email ID and mobile number before submission - the notification clearly states no changes will be entertained after submission.
  • Ensure your photograph and signature meet the prescribed format; wrong or missing uploads can lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Verify your category (UR/EWS/SC/ST/OBCNC/PwBD) carefully before submitting, as category changes are not permitted later.
  • Keep scanned copies of caste certificates, income & asset certificates, and educational documents ready in advance for document verification.
  • Candidates currently employed with HPCL are not eligible to apply for lateral (experienced) positions.
  • Avoid multiple applications - only the latest submitted application will be considered final.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern and Syllabus

The CRE-5 Computer Based Test is a structured, time-bound examination designed to assess both domain knowledge and general aptitude.

CBT Structure

Parameter Detail
Duration 90 minutes
Total Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 400 marks (4 marks per question)
Negative Marking -1 mark per wrong answer (1/4th deduction)
General Knowledge & Aptitude / Computer 20 MCQs
Domain-Specific Questions 80 MCQs
Sections 5 sections × 20 questions × 18 minutes each

Each section is sequential and time-locked - once a section closes, candidates cannot return to it. Candidates must attempt all possible questions within the active section's time window.

Medium of Examination

Posts where the essential qualification is 10th/12th will be examined in bilingual (English and Hindi) medium. Posts requiring bachelor's or higher qualifications, or posts involving specific technical domain knowledge, will be examined in English only.

Qualifying Marks

Category Qualifying Percentage
UR / EWS 40%
OBC 35%
SC / ST 30%
PwBD (all categories) 30%
Ex-Servicemen As per their category

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) higher marks in the domain-specific section; (ii) fewer wrong answers/negative marks; (iii) older date of birth; (iv) alphabetical order of name, then father's name, then mother's name.

Syllabus (Domain Part - Selected Groups)

Group Domain Syllabus
1 Food & Nutrition, Diets
2 General Administration, CCS Rules, FR/SR, Basic Computer
3 General Maths & English

5 Electrical Engineering
12 Pharmacy

34 Nursing

Full syllabus details for all 57 groups are in Section IX of the official DRA.

Skill Test

For selected post groups, a Skill Test is conducted as Stage II for candidates who qualify the CBT. The skill test is qualifying in nature. The final merit list is prepared based on CBT performance, but only among those who pass the skill test for the relevant post.

Posts requiring skill tests include groups such as Junior Administrative Assistant (typing test), Stenographer (stenography test), Programmer (computer skill test), Hindi Translator (translation test), Assistant Security Officer (PST), and Fire Technician (PET & PST). See Annexure-V of the DRA for complete scheme details.

If a candidate qualifies the CBT but fails the skill test, they remain eligible only for posts within the same group that do not require a skill test.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

CRE-5 follows a multi-stage recruitment process. Each stage is mandatory for progression to the next.

Stage 1 - Online Application: Candidates register on www.aiimsexams.ac.in and submit applications by 03 July 2026.

Stage 2 - Application Acceptance: Application status published on 9 July 2026.

Stage 3 - Computer Based Test (CBT): Tentatively 25-27 July 2026 at examination centres across major states/UTs of India.

Stage 4 - Skill Test (where applicable): Conducted after CBT for qualifying candidates in applicable groups. Venue: preferably Delhi/NCR. Date to be notified.

Stage 5 - Choice & Preference: Qualified candidates are invited to exercise institute choices and indicate order of preference. Candidates who fail to exercise choices within the given period will not be considered for any institute.

Stage 6 - Seat Allocation: Allocation is made in order of merit based on choices exercised and eligibility at each participating institute.

Stage 7 - Document Verification: Original certificates verified by the respective AIIMS/Institute on the date notified by them.

Stage 8 - Joining: Selected candidates must report on the date specified in the result/allocation notice. Failure to report will lead to mandatory cancellation of candidature for CRE.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply for AIIMS CRE-5 2026

Applications can only be submitted through the Online Registration Terminal (OTR) at www.aiimsexams.ac.in. Physical documents must not be sent; no correspondence regarding correction in registration will be entertained.

  1. Visit the official website: www.aiimsexams.ac.in
  2. Register through the OTR (One-Time Registration) portal if you have not already done so.
  3. Log in and select the CRE-5 application link.
  4. Fill in all details carefully - name, date of birth, category, qualification, experience, and NOC details if applicable.
  5. Upload photographs, signature, and left thumb impression in the format specified under "Upload Image Instructions."
  6. Select your examination centre preference (state/UT).
  7. Pay the applicable examination fee via Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
  8. Submit the application and download the registration slip for your records.
  9. If you are working in a Government/PSU/Autonomous Body, upload the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from your current employer by 6 July 2026 - failing to do so will prevent you from appearing in the examination.
  10. Check your application status on 9 July 2026 at www.aiimsexams.ac.in.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Required Documents and Certificates

Candidates must have all certificates ready at the time of applying, as no additional time will be granted at document verification. Documents required include:

  • Downloaded Registration Slip and Admit Card
  • Date of Birth certificate (Matriculation certificate or equivalent)
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) - valid and current; OBC NCL certificate must be valid for Financial Year 2026-27 (issued on or after 01 April 2026)
  • EWS certificate issued between 01 April 2026 and 30 June 2026
  • Disability certificate (for PwBD candidates, with minimum 40% benchmark disability)
  • No Objection Certificate from current employer (for Govt./PSU/Autonomous Body employees)
  • Educational qualification certificates
  • Experience certificates mentioning dates, basic pay, and nature of duties
  • Any other certificate required by the respective institute

IBPS Specialist Officer Selection Process 2026

Selection under IBPS CRP SPL-XVI 2026 follows a three-stage process: Online Preliminary Examination, Online Main Examination, and a Common Interview. Only candidates who clear each stage progress to the next, and the final merit list is based on Main Examination and Interview scores combined.

  1. Online Preliminary Examination – Tentatively in August 2026; candidates must clear individual cut-offs in each of four tests.
  2. Preliminary Result – Declared in September/October 2026.
  3. Online Main Examination – Tentatively in November 2026; scores from this stage alone are used for interview shortlisting and final merit.
  4. Main Exam Result – Declared in November 2026.
  5. Common Interview – Conducted by Participating Banks and coordinated by Nodal Banks in November/December 2026; total 100 marks with minimum qualifying marks of 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
  6. Provisional Allotment – Expected in January 2027, based on merit-cum-preference with an 80:20 weightage between Main Exam and Interview.

Exam Pattern Overview

The Preliminary Exam for IT Officer, Agricultural Field Officer, HR/Personnel Officer, and Marketing Officer consists of 100 questions for 125 marks across English Language, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge, to be completed in 80 minutes. The Main Exam for the same posts carries 150 objective questions for 200 marks plus a Descriptive Paper of 25 marks, totaling 225 marks in 155 minutes. Law Officer and Rajbhasha Adhikari have a similar structure but include General Awareness with Special Reference to Banking Industry in place of Quantitative Aptitude.

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in objective tests; no penalty applies for unattempted questions.

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Document Requirements

Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents along with self-attested photocopies at the time of interview, failing which their candidature can be cancelled. Required documents include the interview call letter, system-generated application printout, proof of date of birth, photo identity proof, educational mark sheets/certificates, and category certificates (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/PwBD) as applicable, all in prescribed Government of India formats.

OBC candidates must submit a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026, while EWS candidates need an Income & Asset Certificate valid for the year 2026-27 for financial year 2025-26.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for IBPS CRP SPL-XVI

Many candidates lose their chance at IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 due to avoidable errors during the application process. Being aware of these common mistakes in advance can help ensure a smooth, error-free submission.

  • Applying for multiple posts: A candidate can apply for only one post; multiple applications are summarily rejected.
  • Uploading incorrect photo/signature size: Photos must be 4.5cm × 3.5cm (20-50 KB), and signatures 10-20 KB; oversized or blurred files cause application rejection.
  • Writing the declaration in capital letters: The handwritten declaration must be in the candidate's own handwriting, in English, and NOT in capital letters.
  • Ignoring the Edit Window: Since most fields like Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, and Nationality cannot be edited after submission, double-check all entries before final submission.
  • Missing the fee payment deadline: Applying without completing fee payment within 01.07.2026 to 21.07.2026 renders the form incomplete and invalid.
  • Not retaining photograph copies: Candidates should keep at least 8 copies of the uploaded photograph, as these are required at multiple stages including exam day.

Eligibility Criteria for EIL Fixed Term Engineer Recruitment 2026

Understanding the eligibility conditions for EIL Recruitment 2026 is crucial before you proceed to apply, as failing to meet even one criterion can lead to disqualification at any stage of the process.

Educational Qualification

All candidates must hold a B.E. / B.Tech. / B.Sc (Engineering) degree in the relevant discipline from a recognized university or institution, with a minimum of 60% marks or equivalent CGPA. The exact CGPA equivalents are as follows:

% Marks 10-pt Scale 9-pt Scale 8-pt Scale 7-pt Scale 6-pt Scale 5-pt Scale 4-pt Scale
60% 6.5 5.4 4.8 4.2 3.6 3.0 2.2

Note: Round off percentage to the lower whole number (e.g., 60.9 = 60) and CGPA to the lower decimal (e.g., 6.95 = 6.9).

Experience Requirements

  • Associate Engineer Grade II: Minimum 5 years of post-qualification relevant experience
  • Associate Engineer Grade III: Minimum 9 years of post-qualification relevant experience
  • The cut-off date for experience calculation is 31 May 2026

Age Limit

  • Associate Engineer Grade II: Maximum 37 years as on 31 May 2026
  • Associate Engineer Grade III: Maximum 41 years as on 31 May 2026

Age Relaxation and Concessions

EIL provides age relaxation for several reserved and special categories in line with Government of India directives. This ensures that eligible candidates from diverse backgrounds have a fair opportunity to apply.

Category Age Relaxation
SC / ST 5 years
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
Persons with Disability (PwD) – General / EWS 10 years
PwD – OBC (NCL) 13 years
PwD – SC / ST 15 years
Ex-Servicemen As per GoI rules

PwD Note: Only persons with 40% or more disability are eligible to apply under the PwD category.

Salary and Remuneration for EIL Fixed Term Engineers 2026

One of the most attractive aspects of this EIL recruitment is the competitive consolidated monthly remuneration, which varies by city category and grade. The pay package includes HRA and PF components.

Designation X Category Cities Y Category Cities Z Category Cities
Associate Engineer Grade II ₹80,000/month ₹76,000/month ₹72,000/month
Associate Engineer Grade III ₹96,000/month ₹91,200/month ₹86,400/month

Additional Benefits

Beyond the monthly consolidated pay, EIL also provides a set of value-added benefits to all fixed term engineers:

  • Medical Insurance: Reimbursement of Medical Insurance Premium for self, up to ₹2,00,000 per annum
  • Out-of-Pocket Expenses: Reimbursement for working beyond standard working hours
  • GPAI Scheme: Coverage under the Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme as per Company Policy
  • Travelling Allowance: Payment for official travel outside the place of posting
  • Paid Leave: 2 days of paid leave for each completed month of service

Terms and Conditions of EIL Fixed Term Employment

Before applying, candidates must be aware of the contractual nature of this engagement. EIL's fixed term employment comes with specific conditions that differ from permanent PSU roles.

  • The engagement is purely on a fixed term basis, initially for 2 years, extendable up to a maximum of 3 years from the date of joining, subject to satisfactory performance
  • The engagement will automatically terminate on the expiry of the term unless extended
  • Candidates may be required to work anywhere in India and abroad
  • Only medically fit candidates will be permitted to join
  • No claim for regular/permanent appointment in EIL shall be entertained on the basis of fixed term service
  • Selected candidates must join within 15 days of the announcement of results

Place of Posting

The primary place of posting for all selected candidates will be in the National Capital Region (NCR). However, EIL may deploy engineers anywhere in India or abroad based on project and organizational requirements. Candidates must be prepared for transfers and outstation postings as a condition of this role.

Walk-in Interview Schedule, Venue, and Cities

The walk-in interview for EIL Recruitment 2026 is scheduled across major cities in India, providing candidates from various regions a convenient opportunity to appear. This section covers the tentative timeline and the cities where interviews will be held.

  • Tentative Interview Start Date: 13 July 2026
  • Exact Date: Will be communicated separately via the candidate's registered email ID
  • Interview Cities: Gurugram, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, and Vadodara
  • Interview Timing: Interviews may be held up to 8:00 PM on the same day and, if required, continued the next day. Candidates must make their own arrangements for accommodation.

Candidates based in Chennai will have the option to attend their interview locally, making this a convenient opportunity for Tamil Nadu-based engineers.

Documents Required for the Walk-in Interview

Candidates must carry all required documents in original along with one set of self-attested photocopies. Missing any document may result in disqualification.

Mandatory Documents

  1. 6 copies of the duly filled and submitted online application form with a recent colour photograph affixed
  2. Photo Identity Proof (any one): Driving License / PAN Card / Passport / Voter ID / Aadhar Card
  3. Date of Birth Proof: Matriculation / Class X Certificate / Birth Certificate
  4. Educational Certificates: Mark sheets and passing certificates for Class X, HSC, Degree, and Post Graduation (all semesters/years)
  5. CGPA Conversion Proof from the University/Institute (if applicable)
  6. Experience Certificates (originals) for all experiences mentioned in the application, clearly showing dates of joining and separation, and nature of work
  7. Additional employment proof on demand: Offer letter, confirmation order, pay slips, PF statement, ESI Card, Bank Statement

Category-Specific Documents (if applicable)

  • SC/ST Certificate (in prescribed format from competent authority)
  • Valid OBC (NCL) Certificate (in GoI prescribed format)
  • Valid EWS Certificate
  • Disability Certificate
  • Discharge Certificate and relevant proforma for Ex-Servicemen
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) if currently employed in a Central/State Government or Autonomous Body

Important: If any original document is unavailable on the day of the interview, the candidate will not be considered for further selection.

How to Apply Online for EIL Walk-in Interview 2026

The application process for EIL Recruitment 2026 is entirely online through the official EIL website. Here is the complete step-by-step guide to apply without errors.

Step 1: Visit the official EIL website career section at http://www.engineersindia.com

Step 2: Read all the instructions on the website carefully before beginning the registration

Step 3: Fill in the online form with all accurate details. Round off your percentage to the lower whole number (e.g., 60.9 → 60) and CGPA to the lower decimal (e.g., 6.95 → 6.9)

Step 4: Keep the following scanned documents ready before you begin:

  • Passport-size colour photograph in .jpg/.jpeg format (max 75 KB)
  • Signature in .jpg/.jpeg format (max 25 KB)

Step 5: After submitting the form online, take 6 printouts of the application form, affix a colour photograph on each, and bring them to the walk-in interview

Step 6: Confirm that all details are correct - the cut-off date for experience and age is 31 May 2026

[Apply Online] – Visit https://recruitment.eil.co.in/ between 00:00 hrs on 16 June 2026 and 23:59 hrs on 07 July 2026

[PDF Download Link] – Download the official EIL Recruitment Notification HRD/Rectt./Advt./2026-27/05 from the EIL careers page for complete details.

Important Dates for EIL Recruitment 2026

Staying on top of key deadlines is essential to ensure you don't miss out on this opportunity.

Online Application Closes 30 June 2026 (23:59 hrs)

Walk-in Interview (Tentative) From 13 July 2026

Important Instructions for Applicants

Before you finalize your application, go through these critical instructions issued by EIL to avoid rejection:

  • Only candidates who meet all eligibility criteria should apply
  • Candidates wishing to apply for multiple positions must submit separate online applications for each post
  • Your registered email address must remain valid for at least 24 months from the date of application submission, as all correspondence (including interview intimation) will be sent via email
  • Any updates, corrigenda, or clarifications will be published only on www.engineersindia.com - no separate press notifications will be issued
  • Providing wrong or false information will lead to immediate disqualification
  • No travel or stay allowances will be paid by EIL for attending the interview
  • Any legal disputes will be subject to the jurisdiction of courts in Delhi
  • EIL reserves the right to cancel the advertisement or the selection process without assigning any reason

Note: Fee once paid shall not be refunded under any circumstances. Candidates found to have registered multiple times will be rejected and debarred; fee reimbursement will not be carried out in such cases. In case of unsuccessful payment (money deducted but admit card not generated), wait 7 working days for automatic refund.

Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online

The Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026 online application process has officially commenced for candidates seeking enrollment in the 01/2027 and 02/2027 Batches. Eligible applicants can submit their application forms through the official Indian Navy recruitment portal during the prescribed registration period. Candidates are advised to complete the application process well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues.

The Application Window (Stage I – INET 2/2026) opens on 05 June 2026 and will remain active until 05 July 2026 (05:00 PM). After the application period ends, the Indian Navy will provide a Correction Window on 06 July 2026, allowing candidates to rectify permissible errors in their submitted application forms. Applicants should carefully verify all personal, educational, and communication details before final submission.

To apply online, candidates must first register on the official Indian Navy recruitment website using a valid email ID and mobile number. After registration, they need to fill in the online application form, upload the required documents, and submit the form successfully. It is recommended to keep scanned copies of the photograph, signature, educational certificates, and identity proof ready before starting the application process.

  • Link 1: Apply Online for Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026
  • Link 2: Apply Online for Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026

Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Stage 1 - INET (Indian Navy Entrance Test)

Separate INET exams will be conducted for Electrical and Engineering entries. INET 2/2026 will be conducted in August 2026 with SSC as Exam Partner.

Parameter Details
Mode Computer-based
Total Questions 100 questions of 1 mark each
Language Bilingual - Hindi & English
Type Objective / Multiple Choice
Sections English & General Awareness, Science, Mathematics, and Diploma (Trade Specific)
Duration 1 Hour
Negative Marking 0.25 marks deducted per wrong answer
Passing Criteria Must pass in all sections as well as in aggregate. Indian Navy reserves the right to determine pass marks in each section and in aggregate.
Centre Allocation At the discretion of the Indian Navy; state preference to be indicated by candidate

Stage 2 - Physical Fitness Test (PFT)

Qualifying in PFT is mandatory for selection. Candidates undergoing PFT do so at their own risk.

Gender 1.6 Km Run Squats (Uthak Baithak) Push-ups Bent Knee Sit-ups
Male 06 min 30 sec 20 15 15

Stage 2 - Written Examination

Written exam is conducted only for candidates who qualify PFT. Two separate exams are conducted for Engineering and Electrical streams.

Parameter Details
Total Questions 100 questions of 1 mark each
Language Bilingual - Hindi & English
Type Objective / Multiple Choice
Sections English & General Awareness, Science, Mathematics, and Diploma (Trade Specific)
Duration 1 Hour
Passing Criteria Must pass in all sections as well as in aggregate

Stage 2 - Recruitment Medical Examination

Conducted for all candidates who qualify PFT. Candidates found medically unfit may appeal within 05 days at a designated Military Hospital allocated by the Indian Navy. Medical fitness certificates from hospitals other than designated Military Hospitals will not be considered. No second appeal is permissible.

Stage 3 - Pre-Enrolment Medical at INS Chilka

Pre-enrolment medical formalities of all selected candidates will be conducted at INS Chilka, Odisha. Induction is subject to qualifying in Pre-Enrolment Medical Examination. Candidates not qualifying will be rejected.

Year Customised Package (Monthly) In Hand - 70% (Monthly) Contribution to Agniveer Corpus Fund - 30% (Monthly) Contribution to Corpus Fund by GoI (Monthly)
1st Year ₹30,000 ₹21,000 ₹9,000 ₹9,000
2nd Year ₹33,000 ₹23,100 ₹9,900 ₹9,900

Total Seva Nidhi on completion of 4-year tenure: ₹10.04 Lakhs (Agniveer's contribution + matching GoI contribution). Additional benefits include:

  • Risk, hardship, dress and travel allowances
  • Non-contributory Life Insurance Cover of ₹48 Lakh for the duration of engagement
  • Death Compensation: One-time ex-gratia of ₹44 Lakh (attributable to service) in addition to insurance cover
  • Disability Compensation: One-time ex-gratia of ₹44 / ₹25 / ₹15 Lakh based on 100% / 75% / 50% disability
  • 30 days leave per year; sick leave as per medical advice
  • Medical facilities at service hospitals and CSD provisions
  • No gratuity or pensionary benefits applicable

How to Apply for Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://joinindiannavy.gov.in. No other mode of application will be accepted. Applications can also be uploaded through Common Service Centres (CSC) across the country at a fee of ₹60 + GST (optional facility).

Steps to Apply Online:

  • Visit https://joinindiannavy.gov.in → Click on "Register" → Register as AVR (Apprentice).
  • After successful registration, click on "Login" → AVR (Apprentice) → INET 2/26 → Proceed to apply.
  • Fill in all details carefully. Incorrect declaration of information identified at any stage will result in cancellation of candidature.
  • Upload a recent passport-size colour photograph (taken not before May 2026), size 10 KB to 50 KB; front portrait in light background without head gear (except Sikhs). Date of photograph must be clearly written at the bottom.
  • A live photograph will be captured through the webcam during application form filling.
  • Pay the examination fee of ₹550/- + 18% GST online via net banking / Credit Card / Debit Card / UPI.
  • Give state preference for allocation of INET exam centre. Choice of centre cannot be changed once selected or allotted by the Indian Navy.
  • Candidates will be provided a post-closing correction window. An additional correction window will be activated post INET exam for 2 days.

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded:

  • Matriculation Certificate and Marksheet (proof of date of birth and educational qualification)
  • Diploma Certificate and Consolidated Marksheet from AICTE-recognised Polytechnic Institute
  • Domicile Certificate
  • NCC 'C' Certificate (if applicable) - to be verified through DG NCC
  • Sponsorship Certificate (if applicable) - to be verified through CABS
  • Recent passport-size colour photograph (taken not before May 2026)

Documents to be Produced at INS Chilka at the time of Induction:

  • All original certificates as submitted/uploaded during online application
  • Self-attested copies of all certificates
  • Original NCC 'C' Certificate / Sponsorship Certificate (if held)
  • Police Verification Form duly verified by the Superintendent of Police of respective jurisdiction (from place of domicile or place of residence)
  • Call-up letter / Admit Card

Apply Online at: https://joinindiannavy.gov.in → Register → AVR (Apprentice) → INET 2/26

Call-up Letters cum Admit Card for Stage I - INET 2/2026 will be available for download from https://joinindiannavy.gov.in approximately one week before the online examination. No call-up letter will be sent by post. Only Electronic mode of communication will be used for contacting candidates.

Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026 - Important Instructions

  • Only unmarried Indian male candidates are eligible. Agniveers cannot marry during their entire 4-year tenure; violation will result in dismissal from service.
  • Agniveers are enrolled under the Navy Act 1957 for a period of 4 years. Indian Navy is not obliged to retain Agniveers beyond the engagement period.
  • Up to 25% of each specific batch of Agniveers may be offered permanent enrolment in the Indian Navy as Sailors (Regular Cadre) / Artificers based on performance and organisational requirements. Selection for further enrolment is entirely at the discretion of the Indian Navy; Agniveers have no right to be selected.
  • Agniveers will not be permitted to seek release at their own request prior to completion of the engagement period.
  • Agniveers are not governed by Naval Pension Regulations/Rules and are not entitled to gratuity for the engagement period.
  • Agniveers will not be eligible for Ex-Servicemen status.
  • Candidates declaring incorrect domicile/gender and other details shall not be permitted to appear in the recruitment and their candidature will be cancelled.
  • Candidates reporting 30 minutes after the reporting time for Stage I - INET shall not be allowed to appear in the examination.
  • A candidate's selection pertaining to a particular batch is valid for that batch only. Qualified candidates whose names do not appear in the merit list cannot claim admission for the next batch.
  • Mobile phones or any other communication devices are not allowed inside the examination premises. Infringement will entail disciplinary action including ban from future examinations.
  • Candidates should not submit multiple applications. If more than one application is received, candidature will be cancelled.
  • Minimum height standard is 157 cms. Permanent body tattoos are only permitted on the inner face of forearms (inside of elbow to wrist) and on the reversed side of palm/back (dorsal) side of hand. Tattoos on any other part of the body are not acceptable.
  • Candidates are advised to get their ears cleaned for wax and tartar removed from teeth prior to medical examination.
  • Visual Standards: Uncorrected Vision 6/12, 6/12 | Corrected Vision 6/6, 6/6 | Colour Perception: CP PASS.
  • No enquiry will be entertained regarding this recruitment/enrolment after a period of six months post completion of the recruitment cycle for the respective batch.
  • The terms and conditions given in the advertisement are guidelines only and are subject to change without notice. Further, orders issued by the Government as amended from time to time will apply for selected candidates.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs

Eligibility for forest department jobs depends on the post, state and recruitment authority. Below is a general idea of qualification and age for popular posts like Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer. Candidates should always check the official notification for detailed eligibility criteria.

Education Qualification for Forest Guard, Forester, Ranger

  • Forest Guard / Field Guard / Forest Watcher / Beat Guard: Usually 10th pass or 12th pass from a recognized board, knowledge of local language, and basic physical standards as per state rules.
  • Forester / Section Forest Officer / Deputy Forest Ranger: Generally 12th pass or graduate in any stream or science-related subjects, with physical standards and sometimes driving or technical skills depending on the post.
  • Forest Range Officer (RFO) / Forest Ranger / ACF: Normally graduate degree in Science, Agriculture, Forestry, Environmental Science, Engineering or related disciplines, with higher physical standards and sometimes a competitive exam similar to state PCS level.
  • IFS / Indian Forest Service and senior posts (DCF, CF, CCF, PCCF): Filled through UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination and promotions, requiring a graduate degree and all-India competitive selection.

Age Limit & Relaxation

  • Forest Guard / Forester / Field Guard: Minimum age is usually 18 years and maximum age is around 27–30 years, with age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC, EWS, Ex-servicemen and other categories as per government rules.
  • Forest Range Officer / ACF and higher competitive posts: Age limit often ranges from 21 to 32 years (varies by recruitment), with relaxations for reserved categories.
  • Exact age limit, cut-off date and relaxation details always depend on the particular notification, so candidates should verify from the official advertisement before applying.

Forest Department Jobs Salary Overview
