Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The selection process for Forest Department Jobs 2026 typically includes written examinations, physical tests and document verification. Some posts also conduct medical examination and walking tests due to the demanding nature of field duties.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  • Written Exam: Most Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer recruitments start with a written exam based on objective-type questions (MCQs).
  • PET / PST (Physical Efficiency Test / Physical Standard Test): Candidates who qualify written exam are called for running, walking test, height, chest measurement and other physical parameters as per post and gender.
  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates of age, qualification, caste, residence, sports/NCC and other documents mentioned in the notification.
  • Medical Examination: Many forest posts require medical fitness to ensure candidates can perform field duties in forests, wildlife areas and difficult terrain.

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

Typical syllabus for written exam may include:

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs (national, state-level, environment and forest-related topics)
  • General Hindi / English or regional language (grammar, comprehension, vocabulary)
  • General Mathematics / Quantitative Aptitude (up to 10th or 12th level)
  • General Science and Environmental Studies (forest, wildlife, biodiversity, conservation, climate, basic biology)
  • Reasoning Ability (logical and analytical reasoning)

Exact subject-wise marks, number of questions, negative marking and exam duration will be given in the respective forest department notification.

How to Apply for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Most Forest Department Jobs 2026 applications are accepted either online through official websites or offline via prescribed application forms. Candidates should carefully read the official notification before filling the form.

Online Application Process

  1. Visit the official website of the recruiting body (State Forest Department, State PSC, Staff Selection Board or other government portal).
  2. Find the latest link for Forest Guard / Forester / Forest Range Officer / other forest posts and open the detailed advertisement.
  3. Complete the registration process with basic details like name, mobile number, email ID and verify using OTP if required.
  4. Fill the online application form with personal, educational, address and category information exactly as per documents.
  5. Upload scanned copies of photograph, signature and other certificates in the prescribed format and size.
  6. Pay the application fee online through Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card or UPI as per your convenience.
  7. Finally, submit the form and take a printout or PDF of the submitted application and payment receipt for future reference.

  • Recent passport size photograph and signature (scanned)
  • Class 10th and 12th mark sheets and certificates
  • Degree / Diploma certificates for graduate-level posts
  • Caste / Category certificate (SC, ST, OBC, EWS, etc.)
  • Domicile / Residence certificate if required by the state
  • NCC, Sports, Ex-serviceman and other quota certificates if applicable
  • Valid ID proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, Passport, etc.)

Why Choose Forest Department Jobs?

Forest department jobs are popular among candidates who love nature, wildlife and field work. These jobs offer job security, government benefits and a chance to work in forest conservation, wildlife protection, eco-tourism and community development.

  • Stable government job with regular salary, pension/NPS and allowances
  • Opportunity to work in forests, wildlife sanctuaries, national parks and protected areas
  • Contribution to environment protection, afforestation and biodiversity conservation
  • Good promotion avenues from Forest Guard to Forester, Forest Range Officer and higher posts in many states.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has released Advertisement No. 07/2026 on 25 June 2026, inviting online recruitment applications for 54 posts spread across multiple central government ministries and departments. The vacancies include positions such as Drug Inspector (186 posts), Specialist Grade III Assistant Professor across various medical specialities, Aeronautical Officer (11), Legal Officer (12), Company Prosecutor (18), and several others. Eligible candidates can apply online from 25 June 2026 up to 17 July 2026 at 6:00 PM through UPSC's official portal at upsconline.nic.in. The application fee is ₹25 for General/OBC/EWS male candidates; women, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are fully exempted.

UPSC Advertisement 07/2026 – Eligibility Criteria, Age Limit & Qualifications

Eligibility requirements for UPSC Advt No. 07/2026 vary significantly by post, as these are specialist and technical positions spanning engineering, law, medicine, and administration. All candidates must be Indian citizens. The closing date for submission of the online application - 17 July 2026 - is the reference date for determining eligibility in every respect.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 (Advt 07) – Selection Process

The selection process for UPSC Advertisement No. 07/2026 varies by post. For most posts, it consists of shortlisting based on the online application, followed by a Recruitment Test (RT) or Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) if warranted, and then a Personality Test (Interview). Candidates will be shortlisted for interview based on the information provided in their online application and their performance in the RT, if held.

  1. Online Application Submission: Submit application at upsconline.nic.in by 17 July 2026.
  2. Shortlisting: UPSC shortlists candidates on the basis of information provided in the online application. Incorrect information may lead to rejection through computer-based shortlisting.
  3. Recruitment Test (RT) / Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) – if applicable: For posts where the number of applications is large, UPSC may conduct an RT or CRT before the interview. The test is ordinarily conducted at the following centres: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam.
  4. Personality Test / Interview: Shortlisted candidates are called for interview. Candidates must bring the printout of their online application and all original/self-attested copies of supporting documents.
  5. Final Selection and Appointment: Appointment orders are issued by the respective Ministry/Department. UPSC may grant higher initial pay to candidates adjudged meritorious at the interview stage.

UPSC Advertisement 07/2026 Apply Online – Step-by-Step Guide

The UPSC online recruitment application for Advt No. 07/2026 must be submitted through the official UPSC ORA (Online Recruitment Application) portal at upsconline.nic.in. The last date to apply online is 17 July 2026 at 6:00 PM (1800 Hrs). Candidates are advised to submit their application well in advance to avoid last-minute technical difficulties.

  3. Log in with your credentials.
  4. Select Advertisement No. 07/2026 and choose the specific post/vacancy number you wish to apply for.

Documents Required for UPSC Advt 07/2026 – Interview Stage

Candidates are not required to send any documents to UPSC at the time of application submission. However, all shortlisted candidates called for the interview must carry original documents and self-attested photocopies. Failure to produce required documents at the interview stage will result in disqualification and forfeiture of travelling allowance reimbursement.

  • Photo ID proof (Aadhaar / Voter Card / PAN / Passport / Driving Licence)
  • Date of birth certificate (Matriculation / SSC certificate)
  • Educational qualification certificates (degree, diploma, mark sheets)
  • Experience certificates from all previous/current employers
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) in prescribed proforma from competent authority
  • PwBD disability certificate (minimum 40% disability) in prescribed proforma
  • Certificate for professional registration (where applicable, e.g. NMC/MCI registration for medical posts)
  • Language/publication/NET/GATE/conference/internship certificates if claimed
  • Age relaxation certificate for Ex-Servicemen / Central Government employees in prescribed proforma issued after the date of advertisement
  • Declaration of intimation to Head of Office/Department (for persons already in regular Government service)
  • Documents in language other than Hindi/English must be accompanied by a transcript duly attested by a Gazetted Officer or Notary.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – UPSC Advt 07/2026 Application

Given the large number of posts and the diverse eligibility conditions in UPSC Advertisement No. 07/2026, there are several common errors candidates make. Correcting these proactively can prevent outright rejection before the interview stage.

  • Applying for a post you do not meet the exact qualification for: UPSC shortlists strictly on the basis of declared qualifications. Applying with a "similar" or "equivalent" degree without a formal equivalence order from the competent authority is grounds for rejection. Produce the equivalence order if claiming an equivalent qualification.
  • Entering an inactive or incorrect e-mail address: UPSC sends all interview schedules and document requirements exclusively by e-mail. A wrong email means you will miss the interview call entirely. Double-check before submitting.
  • Submitting incomplete category documents later: All category-based claims (caste, disability, ex-serviceman) must be supportable at the interview stage with original documents in the prescribed UPSC proforma - not general certificates from hospitals or district offices.
  • Not declaring government service: Persons already in regular government service must submit a declaration to UPSC that they have informed their Head of Office in writing. Omitting this can lead to disciplinary consequences.
  • Attempting to withdraw the application after submission: UPSC explicitly states that candidates will not be allowed to withdraw their application once submitted. Apply only if you are genuinely eligible and intend to participate.
  • Bringing a mobile phone to the exam/interview venue: Mobile phones and all electronic devices are strictly banned at UPSC examination/interview halls - even in switched-off mode. Violation results in debarment from future examinations.
  • Waiting until the last day: The portal closes at exactly 1800 Hrs on 17 July 2026. Server congestion near the deadline is common. Complete your application at least 2–3 days in advance.
  • Submitting documents in a language other than Hindi/English without a notarised transcript: Any certificate in a regional language must be accompanied by a transcript attested by a Gazetted Officer or Notary.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Age Relaxation

The standard age relaxations applicable to these posts are as follows. SC candidates receive 5 additional years, OBC candidates receive 3 additional years, and all PwBD candidates receive 10 additional years over and above their category relaxation. For certain posts with a base upper limit of 50 years, the PwBD maximum is capped at 56 years - this applies to the Regional Director (NCONF), Professor Sugar Engineering (NSI), Principal (A&N), and Consultant Ophthalmologist (UT Ladakh). UPSC may relax qualifications and experience at its discretion in writing for candidates otherwise well qualified.

Special Condition - UT Ladakh Posts (Posts 60-70)

All posts under the Administration of the Union Territory of Ladakh are exclusively open to Domiciles of UT Ladakh. A valid Domicile Certificate issued by the Tehsildar under the Ladakh Civil Services Decentralization and Recruitment Rules, 2025 (published in the Gazette of India on 03.06.2025) is mandatory. Two eligible categories exist: Category A (holders of or eligible for Ladakh Resident Certificate) and Category B (children of LRC holders or those eligible). SSC SSA Eligibility Criteria 2026 - Who Can Apply

The SSC SSA / UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025 is open only to regularly appointed Lower Division Clerks (JSA/LDC) serving in the Central Secretariat Clerical Service (CSCS) cadre of DoPT. The crucial date for counting approved service is 1 August 2025. Candidates must satisfy all the following conditions before applying.

Length of Service Requirement

A candidate must have rendered not less than five years' approved and continuous service in the Lower Division Clerk Grade as on 01 August 2025. However, if the candidate was appointed to the LDC grade through a competitive examination (including a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination), the results of such examination must have been declared at least five years before the crucial date and the candidate must have rendered at least four years of approved and continuous service in that grade.

Typewriting Test Condition

Candidates who have been granted exemption from the typewriting test must quote the order number and date of such exemption in the application form.

LDCs on deputation to ex-cadre posts with the approval of the competent authority are eligible to apply if they otherwise fulfill all eligibility criteria. SSC SSA Apply Online 2026 - Step-by-Step Process

The SSC SSA Apply Online 2026 process is carried out in two stages on the SSC portal - first by completing One Time Registration (OTR), then by filling the actual examination application. Candidates who registered on the old SSC website (ssc.nic.in) must create a new OTR on the new website (ssc.gov.in), as the old OTR is not compatible with the new portal. After submitting online, a hard copy must also be forwarded through the department.

  1. Visit the official SSC website: https://ssc.gov.in
  2. Complete One Time Registration (OTR) on the new SSC website if not already done. Click "Register Now" under Login or Register.
  3. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication during OTR as advised by SSC.
  4. After successful OTR, log in using your Registration Number and password.
  5. Click the "Apply" link under "Senior Secretariat Assistant / Upper Division Clerk Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, 2025 (CSCS, DoPT)" in the Live Exam tab.
  6. Select your Service/Cadre as Central Secretariat Clerical Service, DoPT.
  7. Enter your joining date in the feeder service and length of service. Verify eligibility as per Para 30 of the Notice.
  8. Provide details of typewriting test - date passed, roll number, or exemption order details (S. No. 30.1 to 30.4 in the application form).
  9. Capture a live photograph using your webcam or smartphone as instructed - no pre-existing photograph is permitted.
  10. Upload your scanned signature in JPEG format (10-20 KB, dimensions: 6 cm × 2 cm).
  11. Upload mandatory documents: Service Book first page, service particulars, and disability certificate (if applicable).
  12. Preview all entries carefully and submit the application by clicking Submit Application.
  13. Take a printout of the submitted application.
  14. Forward the printed application with required documents through your Head of Department / Head of Office to SSC (NR), New Delhi, reaching by 23 July 2026 (6:00 PM).

Critical reminder: Only those applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission to the examination. Online submission alone is not sufficient.

SSC SSA Exam Pattern 2026 - Scheme of Examination

The SSC Senior Secretariat Assistant exam 2026 is conducted in two parts. Part-I is a Computer Based Examination (CBE) of 200 marks with four subjects, each carrying 50 marks and 50 questions. Part-II is an evaluation of service records (APARs) worth 100 marks. The final rank of the candidate is determined by adding both Part-I and Part-II scores.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (200 Marks)

Subject No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration
Comprehension and General English 50 50 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)
Parliamentary Procedure 50 50
General Knowledge 50 50
Noting and Drafting 50 50
Total 200 200  

All questions are of Objective Type Multiple Choice format. There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer. Candidates must attempt the examination in the language (English or Hindi) opted in the application form, except the "General English" section of the first subject, which must be attempted in English only. No Braille question paper will be provided.

Syllabus for Part-I CBE

Subject Syllabus
Comprehension and General English Simple composition and Applied Grammar
Parliamentary Procedure Simple questions on Parliament sessions and handling of Parliament questions
General Knowledge Current events, everyday observation and general information about India
Noting and Drafting Questions from Chapters 7, 8, and 9 of the latest CSMOP - Guidelines on Noting, Communication, Forms, Channels, Procedure, and Drafting of Communications

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

One hundred marks are earmarked for evaluation of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). Only candidates who qualify Part-I (CBE) will be called for APAR evaluation. Marks from Part-II are added to the Part-I score to determine final merit. Once APARs are evaluated, no request for change in grading will be entertained.

SSC SSA UDC Selection Process 2026

The SSC SSA / UDC selection process 2026 is a two-stage merit-based system. Candidates must first clear the Computer Based Examination and are then shortlisted for APAR evaluation. The final rank is based on the combined aggregate of both stages. This is a competitive examination - success does not confer any right to selection unless the cadre authority is also satisfied about the candidate's suitability.

  1. Stage 1 - Computer Based Examination (Part-I): 200 marks across 4 objective-type subjects. The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks at its discretion.
  2. Stage 2 - Evaluation of Service Records (Part-II): 100 marks based on APAR evaluation. Only Part-I qualifiers are considered.
  3. Final Merit: Aggregate of Part-I (200 marks) + Part-II (100 marks) = 300 marks total. Names of selected candidates will be arranged in order of merit for inclusion in the Select List of SSA/UDC of CSCS cadre.

Tie-Breaking Rules

When two or more candidates secure equal aggregate marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) Marks in CBE overall, (ii) Marks in Comprehension and General English, (iii) Marks in Parliamentary Procedure, (iv) Marks in General Knowledge, (v) Date of birth - older candidate ranked higher, (vi) Alphabetical order of names.

Common Mistakes to Avoid - SSC SSA UDC Apply Online 2026

Based on the structure and requirements of this departmental exam, candidates must avoid the following errors that commonly lead to rejection or disqualification from the SSC Upper Division Clerk Limited Departmental Exam 2026.

  • Skipping the typewriting test details: The application requires specific information about whether the typewriting test was passed or exempted, including roll number and date. Leaving this blank or providing incorrect details is a common reason for application rejection.
  • Not creating a new OTR on ssc.gov.in: The OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is not valid on the new SSC website. Trying to log in with old credentials will fail - create a fresh OTR on ssc.gov.in.
  • Missing the departmental forwarding deadline: Submitting the online application on time is not enough. The printed copy must reach SSC (NR), New Delhi by 23 July 2026 through the HoD/HoO. Many candidates miss this step assuming online submission is sufficient.
  • Uploading a pre-existing photograph: The portal only accepts live photographs captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-taken photo leads to summary rejection of the application.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: The signature must be clearly visible and occupy at least 80% of the allocated box. Miniature, faded, or rotated signatures are the leading reasons for application rejection.
  • Applying without verifying service eligibility: Candidates must confirm that they have rendered at least five years of approved and continuous service in the LDC/JSA grade as on 01 August 2025 before applying.
  • Name/date of birth mismatch: Details in the application - name, father's name, date of birth - must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel candidature.
  • Carrying electronic devices to the exam: Possession of mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3-5 years from all SSC examinations.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: Candidates must ensure their appearance on exam day closely matches the photograph in the application form. Examination staff can deny entry if there is a visible mismatch.

Candidates selected under the SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 for the CSCS Cadre of DoPT will be placed in Pay Level-2 of the 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix. This is a Group 'C' Non-Gazetted post with a pay range of Rs. 19,900 to Rs. 63,200. In addition to the basic pay, candidates will be entitled to allowances (DA, HRA, TA, etc.) as per Central Government rules applicable at the time of appointment.

Selection Process – SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Exam Pattern

The SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 selection process consists of a single-stage Computer Based Examination (CBE) of 180 marks and 3 hours duration. There is no interview or skill test at the selection stage. Final merit is determined solely on the basis of aggregate performance in the CBE, and the Commission prepares a Select List in order of merit up to the number of vacancies.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (CBE) – Exam Pattern

Subject Number of Questions Maximum Marks
Comprehension / General English 60 60
General Knowledge 60 60
CSMOP (Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure) 60 60
Total 180 180
  • Duration: 3 hours (4 hours for candidates eligible for scribe)
  • Question Type: Objective type, Multiple Choice
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer
  • Medium: Candidates must attempt in the language (English/Hindi) opted in the application form, except the "General English" section which must be attempted in English
  • No Braille Question Paper: There is no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates
  • Exam Centre: Delhi-NCR only
  • Compensatory Time: 20 minutes per hour for candidates eligible for scribe/assistive devices

Syllabus for Computer Based Examination

Subject Syllabus Content
Comprehension (English/Hindi) and General English Simple composition, Applied Grammar
General Knowledge Current events, everyday observation, general information about India
CSMOP Simple questions from Chapter No. 5, 6, and 10 of the latest CSMOP — Management of Dak Receipts, File Management System, Records Management

Tie-Breaking Rules

When two or more candidates secure equal aggregate marks, the tie is resolved in the following order:

  1. Marks obtained in 'Comprehension and General English' subject of CBE
  2. Marks obtained in 'General Knowledge' subject of CBE
  3. Date of birth — older candidate ranked higher
  4. Alphabetical order of names

Select List Preparation

After the examination, names of finally selected candidates will be arranged by SSC in order of merit. Selected candidates will be recommended for inclusion in the Select List for JSA/LDC Grade of CSCS Cadre up to the required number of vacancies. This is a competitive examination — success does not confer an automatic right to selection unless the cadre authority also confirms suitability based on conduct in service.

SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Apply Online – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 apply online process is available exclusively at https://ssc.gov.in. This is a two-part process — One-Time Registration (OTR) followed by the Online Application Form. After submission, eligible candidates must also ensure their department forwards the printed hard copy to SSC Northern Region by 23 July 2026. Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission.

  1. One-Time Registration (OTR) on the NEW SSC website: If you have not yet completed OTR on https://ssc.gov.in, do so first. OTR done on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid for the new portal. Keep ready: mobile number, email ID, Aadhaar number (or Voter ID/PAN/Passport/Driving License), and Matriculation (10th class) board/roll number/year of passing. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication for smoother processing. Complete OTR registration within 14 days of starting, or data will be deleted. Save your Registration Number and password.
  2. Log in and apply for the examination: Visit https://ssc.gov.in, log in with your Registration Number and password, click "Apply" under the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 (CSCS, DoPT) listing in the "Live Exam" section.
  3. Fill the Online Application Form: Personal details (S. No. 1–18) auto-populate from OTR. Fill in cadre (Central Secretariat Clerical Service, DoPT), examination year (2025), joining date of feeder service/cadre, length of service, exam medium (English or Hindi), ministry/department/office details, Head of Department and Head of Office details, and complete service history in chronological order.
  4. Upload photograph (live capture) and signature: Capture a live photograph directly through the application module — no pre-existing photograph is required. Ensure plain background, good lighting, no cap/mask/glasses. Upload scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB), dimensions approx. 6.0 cm (width) × 2.0 cm (height). Blurred or miniature signatures lead to rejection.
  5. Upload required certificates: Upload the following in PDF/JPEG format: (i) Service Book first page certified true copy attested by HoD/HoO; (ii) Certified particulars of service (posts held, pay scale, capacity); (iii) Educational qualification certificate (12th standard or equivalent); (iv) Disability certificate (PwBD candidates only).
  6. Preview, declare, and submit: Use the Preview option to verify all entries. Check photograph and signature compliance. Click "I Agree" on the declaration and submit. On successful submission, take a printout of the application form.
  7. Forward hard copy through department (mandatory): Print the submitted application form and attach self-attested photocopies of supporting documents. Submit to your Head of Department/Head of Office for forwarding to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No.12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 23 July 2026 at 6:00 PM (or 30 July 2026 for candidates abroad/Andaman & Nicobar/Lakshadweep).
  8. Download Admit Card: Admission Certificate (AC) will be uploaded on the SSC-NR website (https://sscnr.nic.in) approximately 10 days before the exam; available for download 3–4 days before the exam. AC will NOT be sent by post.

Important: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered. Candidates are advised to submit to their department well before the closing date to ensure timely forwarding. Applications received after the closing date at SSC will be summarily rejected.

Documents Required – Upload Checklist & Hard Copy Submission

Candidates applying for the SSC LDC JSA LDCE 2025 DoPT must upload the following documents at the time of online application and also include self-attested photocopies with the printed application forwarded by the department. All documents must be clear and legible; no original documents should be submitted at this stage.

Documents to Upload Online (and attach with hard copy)

  • Certified true copy of first page of Service Book duly attested by Head of Department/Head of Office — showing name, father's name, husband's name (if applicable), nationality, SC/ST details (if applicable), date of birth in Christian Era (figures and words)
  • Certified particulars of service attested by HoD/HoO — showing posts held, scale of pay, and capacity (substantive/officiating/permanent/temporary)
  • Certificate of essential educational qualification (12th standard or equivalent), if applicable
  • Disability certificate (PwBD candidates) — as per Annexure-VII (Form-V) or Annexure-VIII (Form-VI for multiple disabilities) of the notification

Documents to Carry to Exam Centre

  • Hard copy of Admission Certificate (AC)
  • Departmental Identity Card (Original) issued by employer
  • At least one valid government-issued photo ID — Voter ID, Driving License, PAN Card, Passport, or any Central/State Government-issued photo ID card (for candidates who have not undergone Aadhaar-Based Authentication, also carry two recent passport-size colour photographs and an additional DOB proof)
  • If Photo ID does not show date of birth — carry Matriculation Certificate/Marks Sheet (issued by CBSE/ICSE/State Boards), Birth Certificate, or Category Certificate
  • PwBD candidates availing scribe/assistive devices — carry Medical Certificate (Annexure-II or III) and scribe's photo ID proof (original and photocopy)

Departmental Forwarding Certificate – Role of Head of Department

A unique feature of the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 is the mandatory role of the Head of Department or Head of Office in the application process. The forwarding authority must certify the candidate's service particulars, verify eligibility, sign and stamp the photograph on the printed application, and forward it to SSC Northern Region by the deadline. Without this forwarding, no application will be considered.

The Head of Department/Office must certify the following key points (as per Annexure-VI of the notification):

  • All information given by the candidate is verified and correct as per service records
  • The candidate belongs to the SC/ST community (if claimed), as verified from service records
  • No circumstance renders the candidate unsuitable for promotion to JSA/LDC of CSCS Cadre, DoPT
  • The candidate is a regularly appointed temporary/permanent Group 'C' employee of the participating Ministry/Department/Organization
  • The candidate fulfills all eligibility conditions for the year 2025 considering the crucial date and length of service
  • The candidate has not been debarred or disqualified by any Public Service Commission/SSC/Subordinate Service Commission for any examination/selection
  • A vacancy in the appropriate category is available in the Department/Organization

Critical: The forwarding authority must also sign the candidate's photograph on the printed application form and put a half-seal on the photograph and half on the form. Without this, the application will be summarily rejected.

PwBD / Scribe Provisions – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025

Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) applying for the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 can avail the facility of scribe, technology, or assistive devices. The eligibility for scribe assistance depends on the nature and percentage of disability. Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination will be provided to all candidates eligible for scribe assistance — whether or not they actually avail the facility.

  • Blindness and Cerebral Palsy (40%+): Scribe/technology/assistive devices provided on request in the application form, with upload of disability certificate.
  • Other PwBD categories: Scribe provided on production of a certificate from Chief Medical Officer/Civil Surgeon/Medical Superintendent of a Government health institution (as per Annexure-II) confirming physical limitation to write.
  • PwD with less than 40% disability having difficulty writing: Scribe provided as per OM No. 29-6/2019-DD-III dated 10.08.2022, on production of certificate as per Annexure-III.
  • Scribe/assistive device facility must be opted for in the online application form — it will not be provided without prior intimation.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 DoPT Application

This is a departmental exam with additional procedural requirements not seen in open competitive exams. Many candidates lose their application due to easily avoidable errors. Here are the most critical mistakes to watch for in the SSC JSA LDC CSCS DoPT LDCE 2025:

  1. Using old SSC website OTR for the new website: OTR generated on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid on the new website (ssc.gov.in). Candidates must generate a fresh OTR on the new portal. Using old OTR credentials leads to failure to apply.
  2. Not completing OTR within 14 days: If you start OTR registration but do not complete it within 14 days, your data is automatically deleted. Start and complete OTR well before the application deadline.
  3. Submitting multiple applications: Only ONE application should be submitted. Multiple applications may lead to rejection of the entire candidature.
  4. Not ensuring the department forwards the hard copy on time: Many candidates submit the online application correctly but forget that the department must also forward the printed hard copy to SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Applications received late at SSC — even with valid online submissions — are summarily rejected. Inform your department immediately after applying online.
  5. Forwarding authority not signing the photograph: The Head of Department/Office must personally sign the candidate's photo on the printed application form and put a half-seal across the photo. Without this, the application is summarily rejected — no appeal entertained.
  6. Uploading a photograph of a pre-existing photograph: The application module captures a live photograph. Candidates who photograph a pre-existing printed photo (instead of taking a live capture) will have their applications rejected summarily.
  7. Wearing glasses, cap, or mask in the live photograph: Candidates are specifically instructed not to wear any of these while capturing the live photo. Similarly, the appearance at the exam should match the application photo — changed appearances may deny entry.
  8. Uploading a miniature or blurred signature: The signature must be in JPEG format (10–20 KB), approximately 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm, occupying at least 80% of the signature box. Miniature or blurred signatures are a leading cause of application rejection.
  9. Not indicating the correct medium of examination: Candidates must choose English or Hindi as the medium in the application. The General English section must be attempted in English regardless of medium chosen. This choice cannot be changed after submission.
  10. Changing appearance significantly between application and exam day: Since the exam centre staff verifies appearance against the application photo, significant changes (beard, haircut, spectacles) may raise suspicion and lead to not being allowed to appear.

SSC ASO Eligibility Criteria 2026 – Who Can Apply

The SSC ASO Limited Departmental Exam 2025 is not open to the general public. Only serving government officials of the specific feeder cadres are eligible. The crucial date for counting approved service is 1 July 2025 for both cadres. Candidates must ensure they meet the exact conditions as specified below before applying.

Eligibility for Central Secretariat Service (CSS), DoPT

Any officer in the Upper Division Grade of the Central Secretariat Clerical Service who, as on 01 July 2025, has rendered not less than six years' approved service in that grade is eligible to appear.

Eligibility for Ministry of External Affairs (Cadre Cell)

Officers in the Upper Division Clerk Grade of the MEA Service who, as on 01 July 2025, have (a) successfully completed such mandatory training programme(s) as prescribed by the Ministry of External Affairs and (b) rendered not less than six years' approved service in the grade are eligible.

Disqualification Conditions

A candidate who resigns, quits service, or whose services are terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination. Similarly, candidates appointed to an ex-cadre post or another service on "transfer" without a lien in the SSA/UDC grade are not eligible. This does not apply to candidates on deputation with the approval of the competent authority.

SSC ASO Apply Online 2026 – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC ASO Apply Online 2026 process involves two stages: One Time Registration (OTR) on the SSC portal, followed by filling the actual examination application. Candidates who had registered on the old website (ssc.nic.in) must create a fresh OTR on the new website (ssc.gov.in) as the old OTR is not functional on the new portal.

  1. Visit the official SSC website: https://ssc.gov.in
  2. Click on "Register Now" under the Login or Register section to complete One Time Registration (OTR) if not already done on the new website.
  3. During OTR, opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication as advised by the Commission.
  4. After OTR is complete, log in using your Registration Number and password.
  5. Click the "Apply" link under "Assistant Section Officer / Assistant Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, 2025" in the Live Exam tab.
  6. Fill in departmental details - select your Cadre/Service, joining date of feeder service, and length of service.
  7. Capture a live photograph using webcam/smartphone as prompted (no pre-existing photo allowed).
  8. Upload your scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB, dimensions: 6 cm × 2 cm).
  9. Upload mandatory documents including certified true copy of Service Book (first page) and particulars of service. PwBD candidates must also upload their disability certificate.
  10. Review all entries in the Preview section, accept the declaration, and click Submit Application.
  11. Take a printout of the submitted application form.
  12. Submit the printed copy along with all required documents through your Head of Department / Head of Office to SSC (NR), New Delhi, by 23 July 2026.

Important: Only those candidates whose application is forwarded by their Head of Department / Head of Office will be considered for admission to this examination. Applications submitted directly without departmental forwarding will be rejected.

SSC ASO Exam Pattern 2026 – Scheme of Examination

The SSC Assistant Section Officer Exam 2026 is conducted in two parts. Part-I is a Computer Based Examination (CBE) carrying 300 marks, and Part-II involves Evaluation of Service Records (APARs) carrying 100 marks. The final merit is prepared on the combined aggregate of both parts. There is no separate qualifying exam - this is a competitive examination.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (300 Marks)

Paper Subjects Type Max. Marks Duration
Paper-I (i) General Awareness – flagship programmes and GoI initiatives
(ii) Constitutional provisions and their general application in GoI
(iii) Parliamentary procedures (Manual of Parliamentary Procedures, MoPA instructions)
(iv) Reading Comprehension in English / Hindi
(v) Central Secretariat – Manual of Office Procedure
(vi) Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
(vii) Noting and Drafting		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)
Paper-II (i) Service Rules – Leave Rules, Conduct & CCA Rules, Pension and NPS Rules
(ii) Financial Rules – TA, LTC
(iii) Legislations – RTI Act 2005, POSH Act 2013
(iv) Records Management
(v) Précis Writing		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)

There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks (25%) for each wrong answer in both Paper-I and Paper-II. Candidates must attempt the examination only in the language (English or Hindi) opted in the application form. There will be no question paper in Braille.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

One hundred marks are reserved for evaluation of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). Candidates shortlisted based on their Part-I aggregate performance will proceed to Part-II. Marks from Part-II will be added to determine the final rank. Once APARs have been evaluated, no request for change in APAR grading will be entertained.

SSC ASO Selection Process 2026

The SSC ASO selection process 2026 is a two-stage merit-based system. Candidates must clear the Computer Based Examination before their service records are evaluated. Final selection is strictly based on combined merit - no candidate has a right to selection merely by passing the exam.

  1. Stage 1 – Computer Based Examination (Part-I): Paper-I and Paper-II, each of 150 marks. The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for each paper.
  2. Stage 2 – APAR Evaluation (Part-II): Only candidates who qualify Part-I are eligible. Service records (APARs) are evaluated for 100 marks.
  3. Final Merit: Aggregate of Part-I (300 marks) + Part-II (100 marks) = 400 marks total. Names of finally selected candidates will be arranged in order of merit separately for each cadre.

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal aggregate marks, ties are resolved in the following order: (i) Marks in Paper-I, (ii) Marks in Paper-II, (iii) Date of birth - older candidate ranked higher, (iv) Alphabetical order of names.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC ASO Apply Online 2026

Based on typical departmental exam application processes, candidates should be especially careful about the following errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification.

  • Using Old SSC OTR: OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) will not work on ssc.gov.in. Candidates must create a new OTR on the new website before applying.
  • Not forwarding hard copy through HoD/HoO: Online submission alone is not enough. The printed application must be forwarded by the Head of Department or Head of Office and must reach SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Failure to do this renders the application void.
  • Uploading pre-existing photographs: The portal requires a live photograph captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-existing photo will lead to summary rejection.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: Signatures must occupy at least 80% of the signature box and must be clear. Miniature signatures are the most common reason for rejection.
  • Mismatch in personal details: Name, date of birth, father's name, and mother's name in the application must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel your candidature.
  • Submitting multiple applications: Only one application is allowed per candidate. Multiple submissions may lead to rejection of all applications.
  • Not verifying service eligibility before applying: Candidates must confirm they have completed six years of approved service in the feeder grade as on 01 July 2025 before applying.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: The appearance on exam day must match the photograph in the application form. Examination staff may deny entry to candidates with noticeably different appearances.
  • Carrying electronic devices: Mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3–5 years.

RBI Site Engineer Selection Process 2026

Candidates wondering about the RBI Site Engineer selection process can note that there is no written exam for this recruitment. Selection happens through preliminary screening by a Screening Committee, followed by document verification and a personal interview.

Step-by-Step Selection Methodology

  • Screening & Shortlisting: The Screening Committee may enhance minimum qualification or experience criteria to limit the number of candidates called, in proportion to the number of vacancies. Merely meeting minimum eligibility does not guarantee an interview call.
  • Interview Call Letter: Shortlisted candidates receive their call letter only via email from [email protected] — no postal call letters are issued.
  • Document Verification: Candidates must produce up-to-date Experience Certificates clearly stating nature of duties, dates, duration, level/position, and responsibilities, along with category, age, and qualification proofs.
  • Interview: Candidates discuss their anticipated compensation (within the advertised range) along with previous employer compensation details before the interview, which is considered by the Selection Committee.
  • Final Selection: The RBI Services Board's decision on eligibility, shortlisting, and interview results is final and binding, with no further correspondence entertained.

How to Apply for RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 (Apply Online)

Candidates can apply for RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 only through the official website www.rbi.org.in between 29 June 2026 and 20 July 2026. The process requires registration, document upload, a live photograph capture, and online fee payment before final submission.

  1. Visit www.rbi.org.in, go to Opportunities@RBI > Current Vacancies > Vacancies, and select "Lateral Recruitment of Site Engineers on Full-Time Contract Basis in RBI."
  2. Click "Online Application Form" and select "Click here for New Registration"; enter your name, contact details, and email ID to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  3. Log in and fill in personal, educational, and experience details, using "Save and Next" to verify entries before final submission.
  4. Upload your scanned photograph (20-50KB, JPG), signature (10-20KB, JPG), left thumb impression, and handwritten declaration as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Capture and upload a live photograph using a webcam or mobile phone QR scan during registration.
  6. Upload supporting PDF documents (20KB-500KB each) for age, category, educational qualification, and work experience proof.
  7. Click "Complete Registration" only after verifying all details, since no changes are allowed afterward.
  8. Proceed to the "Payment" tab and pay the applicable fee via debit card, credit card, net banking, IMPS, or mobile wallet, then click "Submit."

Candidates should submit only one application per post; in case of multiple submissions, only the last completed application with the higher Registration ID (RID) will be considered, and fees paid against one RID cannot be adjusted to another.

RBI Site Engineer Salary and Pay Scale 2026

Selected candidates under RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 receive a monthly consolidated compensation based on their post level, along with housing allowance applicable at the centre of posting. The Selection Committee can offer a higher starting amount within a defined range based on the candidate's qualification, experience, and skill set.

The monthly compensation, excluding housing allowance, increases by 7% on successful completion of every 12 months during the contract period, including any extension. This compensation is subject to applicable tax deduction at source, and contract appointees are not eligible for superannuation, separation benefits, or any other allowance or medical benefit beyond what is specified.

Candidates applying for RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 must upload several documents in PDF format during the online application process, with each clearly supporting their claims for age, category, qualification, and experience. Missing or unclear documents can lead to rejection at the verification stage.

  • Proof of age (PDF format)
  • Category certificate for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD/EWS, where applicable, dated on or before the closing date
  • Educational qualification documents (B.Tech/M.Tech certificates and mark sheets)
  • Up-to-date Experience Certificate clearly stating nature of duties, dates, duration, level/position, and responsibilities
  • Scanned photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, 20-50KB, JPG/JPEG)

  • Live photograph captured via webcam or mobile during registration

OBC candidates must specifically produce a Non-Creamy Layer certificate based on income for FY 2023-24, 2024-25, or 2025-26, issued on or after 01 April 2026 but before the closing date of 20 July 2026.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for RBI Site Engineer 2026

Many candidates risk rejection due to avoidable errors during the RBI Site Engineer online application process. Reviewing these common mistakes beforehand can help ensure your application is processed without issues.

  • Writing the declaration in capital letters or another language: The handwritten declaration must be in English, in the candidate's own handwriting, and not in capital letters — non-compliant declarations make the application invalid.
  • Expecting age relaxation: Unlike many government recruitments, RBI has explicitly stated no age relaxation is available for any category in this notification, so candidates must meet the 40-65 year window strictly.
  • Submitting multiple incomplete applications: If multiple applications are filed for the same post, only the last completed one with the higher Registration ID is considered, and the fee from the earlier RID is not adjusted.
  • Uploading documents in the wrong format: Photograph and signature must be JPG/JPEG, while all other supporting documents must be in PDF format within the specified size limits.
  • Not informing current employer: Government/PSU employees must submit an undertaking confirming they have informed their employer in writing about applying, or their candidature may be rejected.
  • Ignoring OBC NCL certificate dating: OBC candidates need a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01 April 2026 — older certificates based on different financial years won't be accepted.

RCF Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria - Qualification and Age Limit

The eligibility criteria for RCF Officer Recruitment 2026 vary significantly by post and grade. All qualifications must be from UGC/AICTE-recognized universities or institutions, and experience is calculated as of 01 March 2026.

Officer (Finance) - E1 Grade

Candidates must hold either a CA/CMA qualification or a full-time graduation degree in Commerce/Accounting/Finance (B.Com, BMS, BAF, BBA) along with a 2-year full-time MBA/MMS/PGDM/PGDBM with specialization in Finance. M.Com alone is not accepted. Minimum 60% in the final year of the qualifying post-graduation degree is required (55% for SC/ST). No percentage criterion applies for CA/CMA holders. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification executive-level experience in accounting, auditing, budgeting, or taxation is required. Training, internship, and articleship periods do not count toward experience. Age limit: SC/ST - 39 years; OBC (NCL) - 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (HR) - E1 Grade

A full-time graduation degree in any discipline plus a 2-year full-time post-graduation degree/diploma/equivalent master's degree with specialization in HR/Personnel/Social Work/Welfare/Industrial Relations/Labour Studies from a UGC/AICTE institution is required. Minimum 55% for SC category candidates in the final year of the post-graduation. Additional qualification in law and proficiency in Marathi are preferred. Minimum 2 years of experience in HR departments covering labour administration, industrial relations, and grievance handling is required. Age limit: SC - 39 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (Medical) - E1 Grade

MBBS with completed internship and registration with the Medical Council of India or State Medical Council is mandatory. Preference is given to candidates with a Certificate Course in Industrial Health (3 months) or AFIH recognized by DGFASLI, or a 2-year recognized Diploma in Anaesthesiology. Minimum 2 years of experience (excluding internship) in a hospital of 25 beds or more is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) - 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Senior Manager (CC Lab) - E5 Grade

Candidates must hold either a Ph.D. in Chemistry from a UGC/AICTE-approved institution or a 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Chemical Engineering/Petrochemical Engineering/Chemical Technology (minimum 60% aggregate). Preference is given to Ph.D. holders. Minimum 17 years of relevant experience in academics or research is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) - 52 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (Legal) - E1 Grade

A regular full-time LLB degree or a 5-year integrated Law degree from a recognized Indian university is required, with a minimum of 60% in the final year of LLB. At least 2 years of relevant experience in PSU/Government/Autonomous Bodies/MNC/Private Organization/Law firms or practicing as an Advocate is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) - 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Assistant Engineer (Electrical) - E0 Grade

A 3-year full-time Diploma in Electrical/Allied Electrical Engineering/Technology from a UGC/AICTE institution is required, with a minimum of 60% in the final year. Sandwich-pattern diploma holders (3½ or 4 years) are also eligible. Minimum 16 years of post-diploma relevant working experience is required. Age limit: UR - 42 years; OBC (NCL) - 45 years as on 01.03.2026.

Engineer (Electrical) - E1 Grade

A 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Electrical/Electrical and Power/Electrical Power Engineering, or a 3-year B.E./B.Tech acquired after a 3-year full-time Diploma, or a Dual/Integrated Degree in Electrical Engineering - all from UGC/AICTE institutions with minimum 60% aggregate - is required. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification field experience in HT/LT electrical equipment maintenance in fertilizer, chemical, refinery, petrochemical, cement, or power plant industries is required. Age limit: UR - 34 years; OBC (NCL) - 37 years; PwBD (UR) - 44 years; PwBD OBC (NCL) - 47 years as on 01.03.2026. One PwBD (OH - one lower limb affected) vacancy is available.

Senior Engineer (Electrical) - E2 Grade

Same educational qualification as Engineer (Electrical) - minimum 60% B.E./B.Tech in Electrical Engineering from UGC/AICTE institutions. Minimum 4 years of post-qualification field experience in HT/LT electrical equipment maintenance is required. Age limit: UR - 36 years; OBC (NCL) - 39 years as on 01.03.2026.

Deputy Manager (Electrical) - E3 Grade

Same educational qualification as above (B.E./B.Tech Electrical, minimum 60%) from UGC/AICTE institutions. Minimum 8 years of post-qualification field experience in HT/LT electrical equipment maintenance is required. Age limit: UR - 38 years; OBC (NCL) - 41 years as on 01.03.2026.

Engineer (Civil) - E1 Grade

A 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Civil Engineering or allied Civil specializations (Construction Engineering, Civil Technology, etc.) with minimum 60% from UGC/AICTE institutions is required. Lateral entry B.E./B.Tech after a 3-year Diploma is also eligible. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification experience in process industries such as fertilizers, chemicals, or refineries is required. Age limit: UR - 34 years as on 01.03.2026.

Senior Engineer (Civil) - E2 Grade

Same qualification as Engineer (Civil) - B.E./B.Tech Civil Engineering (60% minimum). Minimum 4 years of post-qualification experience in process industries preferably in fertilizers, chemicals, or petrochemicals is required. Age limit: UR - 36 years as on 01.03.2026.

Selection Process - RCF Recruitment 2026

The selection process for RCF Ltd 2026 differs by grade. Understanding the process in advance helps candidates prepare effectively for each stage.

For the E0 Grade (Assistant Engineer - Electrical), selection is through a Skill Test consisting of three components: Practical Job Knowledge and Handling of Technical Equipment (70 marks), Safety Awareness and Computer Knowledge (20 marks), and Communication Skills (10 marks) - totalling 100 marks. Candidates must score a minimum of 60 marks (55 marks for SC/ST) to qualify. The Skill Test is of a qualifying nature.

For E1 Grade and above (all Officer, Engineer, Senior Engineer, Deputy Manager, and Senior Manager posts), selection is through a Personal Interview. The interview carries 100 marks distributed as: Subject Knowledge (50 marks), Nature of Experience (20 marks), Personality and Communication Skills (15 marks), and General Awareness/Computer Knowledge/Additional Qualification (15 marks). Candidates must secure a minimum average of 50% marks to qualify the interview.

A waiting list is also maintained - in the ratio of 1:2 for up to 5 vacancies and 1:1 for more than 5 vacancies - valid for one year from the date of empanelment.

All outstation candidates called for Skill Test or Personal Interview are reimbursed to-and-fro III-tier AC train/bus fare from their correspondence address to the interview/test venue.

Common Mistakes to Avoid - RCF Bharti 2026

Many candidates lose their eligibility due to avoidable errors in the application process. The following original guidance is based on common pitfalls in PSU recruitment applications.

Uploading documents in wrong formats is one of the most common rejection reasons - ensure photographs are in JPG/JPEG at 165×125 pixels and all supporting documents are in PDF format. Candidates often assume M.Com qualifies for the Finance Officer post - the notification explicitly states M.Com is not accepted; an MBA/MMS/PGDM with Finance specialization is mandatory. Failing to convert CGPA to percentage before submission causes frequent rejections; contact your university for the official conversion formula and attach a copy at interview. OBC candidates whose most recent Non-Creamy Layer certificate was issued before 1 April 2025 will not be accepted - the notification specifically requires a certificate issued on or after 1 April 2025.

Counting internship, articleship, or training periods as work experience is not permitted - only post-qualification executive experience counts. Name mismatches between the application and photo identity proof result in disqualification from the Skill Test or Interview - use your name exactly as it appears on your Matriculation certificate. Government-employed candidates must carry a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their present employer at the time of interview or their candidature will be rejected.

One of the unique aspects of this ISRO ISTRAC Bharti 2026 is that vacancies are distributed across multiple ISRO facilities and remote locations across India. The posting location varies by post code and even by individual vacancy within the same post code. Candidates must carefully check the posting location details for each vacancy before applying, as transfers to other stations may or may not be possible after appointment.

Posting locations mentioned in the notification include: ISTRAC Bengaluru, MCF Hassan (Master Control Facility), NSRAC, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, SDSC SHAR (Satish Dhawan Space Centre) in Andhra Pradesh, and Thiruvananthapuram. For Technical Assistant (Electronics) under Post Code 005, there are 35 vacancies distributed across all these locations. Candidates residing in or willing to relocate to these locations should apply accordingly.

Common Mistakes to Avoid - ISRO ISTRAC Apply Online 2026

Applicants for ISRO ISTRAC Recruitment 2026 should be careful about the following common errors that can lead to rejection or disqualification.

  • Applying for the wrong post code: Each post has distinct qualifications. For example, Post Code 007 (Scientific Assistant - Computer Science) and Post Code 008 (Scientific Assistant - Mathematics) have different subject requirements. Verify the correct post code before submitting.
  • Not verifying posting location: Some post codes have vacancies at multiple locations. Ensure you are aware of where the specific vacancy is posted, as all posts are temporary and location-specific.
  • Incorrect experience certificate for Cook-A: The notification explicitly states that experience certificates from individuals will not be accepted for Post Code 010 (Cook-A). Only certificates from established hotels or canteens are valid.
  • Not checking ITI trade name carefully: For Technician-B posts, the ITI/NTC/NAC must specifically be in the notified trade. A closely related trade that is not listed (e.g., a general electrical trade instead of Electronics Mechanic) may not be accepted.
  • Missing the application deadline: The online portal closes at 5:00 PM on 20 July 2026. Waiting until the last day risks technical failure. Apply at least 2-3 days before the deadline.
  • Uploading blurred documents: All uploaded certificates, photos, and signatures must be clearly legible. Low-resolution scans are a leading cause of application rejection.
  • Incorrect age calculation: Age must be calculated as on 13 July 2026, not the notification date or application date. Double-check your eligibility before applying.
  • Not reading the PwBD reservation details: Some post codes have specific PwBD category reservations (e.g., HH for Post Code 007, OH/CH for Post Code 003). Only the specified disability categories are eligible under those reservations.

Eligibility Criteria – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

Eligibility for the 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026 is restricted to two specific candidate groups: ex-servicemen of the Armed Forces, and ex-women employees (including premature retirees) of the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF & CC) and the State Forest Department. Both groups must meet the service, medical, and character conditions listed below.

  • Enrolment window: Candidates should be enrolled within 5 years from their date of retirement.
  • Medical Category: SHAPE-I is required.
  • Character: Must be Exemplary or Very Good.
  • Qualification: Ex-servicemen must be of Indian Domicile and pension holders only. Ex-women employees (including premature retirees) of MoEF & CC and the State Forest Department must have rendered a minimum of 20 years of service in MoEF & CC or the State Forest Department.
  • Conduct: Candidates should not be involved in any civil or police cases.

Candidates wondering about the recruitment procedure can note that it differs by category. Ex-servicemen Male candidates undergo a physical fitness test - a 1.6 km run, pull-ups, a 9 ft ditch, and balance, all assessed as per age criteria - followed by a medical test and interview for those shortlisted. Ex-women employees of MoEF & CC and SFD instead go through an interview by the Board of Officers (BOO), a proficiency test in afforestation-related activity and nursery management conducted by the BOO, and a medical examination.

Selection Process – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

Selection under the 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026 follows a multi-stage process spread across the rally dates, beginning with document verification and ending with medical examination and interview of shortlisted candidates. The exact process differs slightly depending on whether the candidate is an ex-serviceman or an ex-woman employee of MoEF & CC/SFD.

  1. Online Registration (before the rally): Register at www.130ta.com as per the eligibility criteria and terms of engagement, or plan to report directly with documents if registration is not possible.
  2. Document Verification (03 August 2026): Original documents are checked at Devkatiya Ground, Pithoragarh.
  3. Physical Fitness Test (04 August 2026, for Ex-servicemen Male): 1.6 km run, pull-ups, 9 ft ditch, and balance test, assessed as per age criteria.
  4. Interview & Proficiency Test (for Ex-women employees of MoEF & CC/SFD): Interview by the Board of Officers along with a proficiency test in afforestation-related activity and nursery management.
  5. Medical Examination & Interview of Shortlisted Candidates (05 to 08 August 2026): Candidates who clear the physical test or BOO assessment undergo medical examination and a final interview.
  6. Merit-based Enrolment: Enrolment is purely on merit basis and is subject to the number of vacancies actually available in each trade.

  4. Report to Devkatiya Ground, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand on 03 August 2026 at 0600 hrs with all original documents listed in the documents-required section.
  5. Undergo document verification on Day 1, followed by the physical test/BOO assessment on Day 2, and medical test & interview (if shortlisted) between 05 and 08 August 2026.

Documents Required – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

Candidates must carry all original documents to the recruitment rally, as the document set differs for ex-servicemen male candidates and ex-women employees of MoEF & CC/SFD.

Ex-servicemen Male

  • PPO (Pension Payment Order) & Discharge Book
  • Domicile Certificate / Aadhaar Card
  • Eight copies of photograph

Ex-women Employees of MoEF & CC and State Forest Department

  • Certificate from the concerned department confirming 20 years of service rendered by the candidate
  • Domicile Certificate / Aadhaar Card
  • Eight copies of coloured photograph

Salary & Engagement Terms – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

This is not a regular salaried government job, and the notification does not specify a fixed monthly salary or pay scale. Candidates are paid only for the period they are actually embodied (engaged in service), which depends on the requirement of the funding agency and the direction of the unit or higher headquarters in a given year.

  • Ex-servicemen are initially engaged for a period of 2 years, extendable by 1 year at a time, subject to satisfactory performance.
  • As per Ministry of Defence letter No. PC to MF 68640/ECO/Gen/TA-2/513/US/D(GS-III)/2018 dated 30 October 2018, service rendered in Infantry Battalion (TA) Ecological units by ex-servicemen is not admissible to pension, increment, or gratuity.
  • Service of ex-servicemen and ex-women employees in these Ecological units is treated as rehabilitation and is not at par with service of soldiers in the Regular Army or Territorial Army.
  • The organisation does not provide or promise permanent employment of any kind.
  • Authorities conducting the rally are not responsible for any accident or injury to candidates during the recruitment rally.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026

Candidates preparing for the 130 INF BN TA ECO KUMAON Recruitment Rally 2026 should watch out for the following avoidable errors that can affect their candidature.

  • Assuming this is a permanent government job: The notice explicitly states that no permanent employment is provided or promised; engagement is for an embodied period only.
  • Carrying photocopies instead of originals: Document verification requires original PPO/Discharge Book, pension order, and domicile/Aadhaar documents - not photocopies alone.
  • Missing the photograph count: Both categories must carry exactly eight copies of photographs (coloured for ex-women employees) - carrying fewer can delay verification.
  • Skipping online registration without a backup plan: If registration at www.130ta.com fails, candidates must still be ready to report in person on 03 August 2026 at 0600 hrs with all documents.
  • Not checking the 5-year enrolment window: Ex-servicemen must be enrolling within 5 years from their date of retirement; applying outside this window makes a candidate ineligible.
  • Expecting pension or gratuity benefits: Service in this Ecological battalion is explicitly not admissible to pension, increment, or gratuity as per the 2018 Ministry of Defence letter.
  • Arriving unprepared for the physical test: Ex-servicemen male candidates should be ready for the 1.6 km run, pull-ups, 9 ft ditch, and balance test on Day 2, assessed as per age criteria.
