Eligibility Criteria - Qualification & Age Limit

The CCRUM Ayush Job 2026 eligibility varies significantly by post group. Candidates should verify their qualification carefully against the specific post before applying, as merely meeting one criterion is not sufficient.

Group A - Research Officers

Research Officer (Unani): PG Degree (MD or MS) in Unani System of Medicine from a university/institution recognized by NCISM (formerly CCIM), plus enrolment on the Central Registrar of NCISM/CCIM or State Register of Unani/ISM. Age: up to 40 years (Government servants get 5 years' relaxation).

Research Officer (Pathology): MD in Pathology from an MCI-recognized university. Enrolment on Central Register of MCI or State Register of Medical Council. Age: up to 40 years.

Research Officer (Physiology): Master's Degree in Molecular Biology / Biotechnology / Human Genetics / Genetics Engineering from a recognized institution, plus 3 years' post-Master's research experience OR a Ph.D. in the relevant subject. Age: up to 40 years.

Group B - Key Posts

Asst. Research Officer (Pharmacology): M.Sc. in Pharmacology or M.V.Sc from a recognized university. Age: up to 30 years.

Asst. Research Officer (Pharmacognosy/Botany): Master's Degree in the concerned discipline plus 3 years' research/teaching experience OR a Ph.D. in the relevant discipline. Age: up to 35 years.

Staff Nurse: B.Sc. (Hons) Nursing / Regular B.Sc. Nursing / Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing OR Diploma in General Nursing & Midwifery from a recognized institution, registered as Nurse/Nurse & Midwife with State Nursing Council, plus 1 year's experience in a minimum 50-bed hospital. Age: up to 35 years.

Accounts Officer (HQ): Degree from a recognized university plus 3 years' experience in Cash, Accounts, and Budget work in a Government Office / PSU / Autonomous Body. Age: up to 30 years (5-year relaxation for CCRUM employees).

MLT: Bachelor's Degree in Medical Laboratory Science with 2 years' relevant experience. Age: up to 35 years.

Library & Information Assistant: Degree from a recognized university plus Degree in Library Science. Age: up to 28 years.

Group C - Key Posts

UDC: Degree from a recognized university. Age: between 18 and 27 years.

LDC: 12th class pass with typing speed of 35 wpm in English or 30 wpm in Hindi on computer. Age: between 18 and 27 years.

Stenographer Grade-III: Matric/equivalent plus shorthand speed of 80 wpm and typewriting speed of 40 wpm. Age: up to 28 years.

Staff Car Driver: Matriculation pass, valid driving license for Motor Cars/LMV, 3 years' motor car driving experience, knowledge of vehicle maintenance. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

MTS: Matriculation/equivalent pass OR ITI pass in relevant subject. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

Compounder: Matric or equivalent plus Certificate of Training as Compounder in Unani System of Medicine (minimum 1 year), plus 2 years' experience preferably in a Unani Dispensary/Hospital. Age: 28 years and below.

Pharmacist: 10+2 with Science plus 2-year Diploma in Pharmacy plus registration with State/Central Pharmacy Council. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

Age Relaxation Summary

Candidates wondering about age relaxation can note the following: SC/ST candidates get 5 years' relaxation, OBC-NCL candidates get 3 years, PwBD (UR) candidates get 10 years, PwBD (OBC-NCL) candidates get 13 years, and PwBD (SC/ST) candidates get 15 years. The maximum age after all cumulative relaxations shall not exceed 56 years. Candidates domiciled in Jammu & Kashmir between 1 January 1980 and 31 December 1989 are also eligible for 5 years' relaxation.

Application Fee - CCRUM Recruitment 2026

The CCRUM 2026 application fee structure is divided into a non-refundable Processing Fee (applicable to all candidates) and an Examination Fee (waived for exempted categories). SC/ST, PwBD, EWS, Women candidates, and Ex-Servicemen are exempt from the Examination Fee but must still pay the Processing Fee.

Payment is accepted only through the online payment gateway via Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. Cash, Demand Draft, and Postal Orders are not accepted. The fee is inclusive of GST; bank charges will be levied additionally depending on the payment mode.

Selection Process - CCRUM Ayush Vacancy 2026

The CCRUM 2026 selection process differs by post group. Group A candidates face both a written test and an interview, while Group B and C candidates are selected primarily through the Computer Based Test.

Group A Posts (Research Officers):

  • Online CBT - 70 marks (subject knowledge + research methodology + general awareness)
  • Interview - 30 marks
  • Shortlisting ratio: 1:5 for 1 vacancy, 1:4 for 2 vacancies, 1:3 for 3 or more vacancies
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 25% for SC/ST/PwBD; 30% for all others

Group B & C Posts:

  • Online CBT - 100 marks
  • Skill Test (mandatory and qualifying) for LDC, Stenographer Grade-III, Staff Car Driver, and wherever applicable
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 25% for SC/ST/PwBD; 30% for all others

Negative Marking: There is a 0.25 mark deduction per wrong answer in the CBT for all posts except MTS, where there is no negative marking.

Exam Duration: 100 minutes for all candidates (Group A, B & C). PwBD candidates eligible for a scribe receive 130 minutes (100 + 30 compensatory minutes).

Exam Centers: New Delhi/Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Guwahati.

Tie-Breaking Rules: In case of equal marks, tie-breaking follows this order: older age ranked higher → higher subject marks → higher marks in second part of syllabus → earlier degree/diploma completion → higher final aggregate percentage.

Exam Syllabus at a Glance

The CCRUM CBT syllabus is post-specific. Every paper follows a common structure: subject knowledge (70 marks) + research methodology/relevant technical knowledge (20 marks) + general awareness/IT & computing (10 marks) for Group B and C posts. Group A post papers total 70 marks (subject: 40 + research methodology: 20 + general awareness/IT: 10), followed by an interview of 30 marks. MTS and Staff Car Driver follow SSC's MTS/Matric-level examination syllabus.

How to Apply - CCRUM Recruitment 2026 Online Application

All applications for CCRUM Bharti 2026 must be submitted online only through the official CCRUM website. No documents or application forms need to be sent to CCRUM by post or mail.

  1. Visit www.ccrum.res.in or www.ccrum.ayush.gov.in and go to the "Advertisement/Vacancy" tab.
  2. Create a new account (Step I): Enter your full name (as per Matriculation Certificate), father's name, mother's name, gender, date of birth, mobile number, valid email ID, and Government ID proof. Verify via OTP.
  3. Complete your profile (Step II): Log in with your Reference Number and Password. Upload photograph, signature, caste certificate, disability certificate (if applicable), basic qualification certificates, and other relevant documents.
  4. Apply for the post (Step III): Select the post(s) you wish to apply for, fill in post-specific information, and upload post-specific documents.
  5. Pay the fee: You will be redirected to the payment gateway. Pay via Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI. Download the payment acknowledgement slip.
  6. Download your application form in PDF format from the Dashboard for future reference.

Important: Details entered during account creation (Step I) cannot be modified at any later stage. Candidates applying for multiple posts must use the same login reference number and pay the fee separately for each post.

Modification Window

After the application window closes, CCRUM provides a Modification Window from 3 August 2026 (10:00 AM) to 5 August 2026 (23:59 hrs). A modification fee of ₹300 per attempt per post is charged. Note that account creation details from Step I cannot be changed through this window. If a modification makes a candidate ineligible for the post, the change will not be permitted.

Salary / Pay Scale

The CCRUM Recruitment 2026 offers 7th CPC pay structure with NPA (Non-Practising Allowance) for Group A medical posts as per Government of India rules. Selected candidates are placed on probation for two years, extendable at the discretion of the competent authority, and will be governed by the New Pension Scheme (NPS). All posts carry All India transfer liability; candidates must be willing to serve at any of CCRUM's 24 Institutes/Centers across India.

Documents Required

Candidates should keep the following documents ready before starting the CCRUM online application 2026. All documents must be scanned and uploaded in JPEG/JPG or PDF format as specified.

  • Latest passport-size colour photograph (50–100 KB, JPEG/JPG), taken in 2026
  • Signature on white paper with black ink pen (50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG)
  • Caste/Category Certificate in Central Government format (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD/EWS)
  • Disability Certificate issued by Competent Authority (for PwBD candidates)
  • Discharge Certificate (for Ex-Servicemen)
  • Educational qualification certificates with mark sheets
  • Valid Government photo ID proof (Voter ID, Passport, PAN Card, or Driving License)
  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates already in Government service)
  • Each document file: between 100 KB and 1000 KB in PDF/JPG/JPEG format

Common Mistakes to Avoid

These are avoidable errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification in CCRUM recruitment:

  • Entering wrong details at account creation: Name, date of birth, and gender entered at Step I cannot be changed under any circumstances. Cross-check with your Matriculation Certificate before submitting.
  • Not checking the OBC certificate date: Your OBC (NCL) certificate must have been obtained within 3 years before the closing date of application. An outdated certificate will result in disqualification.
  • Applying through offline modes: Applications submitted by post, email, or courier are rejected outright without any communication.
  • Uploading blurry or cut documents: All uploaded documents must be clear, complete, and within the specified file size limits.
  • Missing the payment confirmation step: Your application is only considered submitted after successful payment. Always ensure the payment status reads "Payment Received."
  • Not downloading your application form: After Step III, download and preserve your application form PDF and payment receipt from the Dashboard for future reference.
  • Using electronic devices in the exam hall: Mobiles, smart watches, calculators, earphones, and Bluetooth devices are strictly prohibited. Violation leads to a ban of at least 5 years from CCRUM exams.
  • Applying for multiple posts with different logins: Candidates must use the same reference number for all posts. Creating multiple accounts is not permitted.

Who Can Apply? - NIACL Apprentice 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Understanding the eligibility criteria is the first and most critical step before applying. Here is a detailed breakdown of all conditions you must satisfy.

Nationality

All applicants must be citizens of India.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government.

Crucially, the final year mark sheet date must fall between January 1, 2022 and June 1, 2026 (both dates inclusive). Graduates who passed before January 1, 2022, or after June 1, 2026, are not eligible.

Prior Apprenticeship Condition

  • Candidates must not have previously undergone apprenticeship training under the Apprentices Act 1961 - either with NIACL or any other organization.
  • Candidates currently pursuing an apprenticeship anywhere are also ineligible.
  • Candidates with one or more years of job experience after graduation are not eligible.

Step-by-Step Process

2. Note Your NATS Enrolment Number After applying on NATS, you will receive a unique NATS enrolment number. This is mandatory for the next step.

3. Apply on BFSI SSC Portal Go to https://beep.bfsissc.com/candidate_login. Fill in personal details, upload documents, enter your NATS enrolment number, choose your preferred state, and pay the examination fee.

Selection Process - How NIACL Apprentices Are Chosen

Stage 2 - Regional Language Test & Document Verification

Candidates who clear the online written test are shortlisted in 3× the number of available seats per state per category for this stage.

  • Candidates who studied the regional language of their chosen state in Class 10 or 12 are exempt from the language test.
  • All others must demonstrate proficiency (reading, writing, speaking, and understanding) in the specified local language of the state.
  • Candidates failing the language test cannot be engaged as apprentices.

Leave Policy

  • Apprentices are entitled to all company-observed public holidays

Training Duration & Certification

  • Training period: 12 months
  • On completion, apprentices undergo an assessment (theory by BFSI SSC + practical by NIACL)
  • Successful candidates receive an Apprenticeship Certificate from BFSI SSC

Indian Navy Officer Recruitment 2026 – Eligibility Criteria

Understanding the Indian Navy SSC officer eligibility 2026 is the most critical step before filling the application. Eligibility differs by branch - both in terms of educational qualification streams and date-of-birth range. Candidates must meet conditions of nationality as laid down by the Government of India.

Educational Qualification – Branch-wise

The minimum educational requirement for most branches is a BE/B.Tech degree with minimum 60% marks in the relevant discipline. Here is a branch-wise summary of qualification requirements:

  • Executive Branch (GS(X)/Hydro): BE/B.Tech in any discipline with minimum 60% marks.
  • Pilot: BE/B.Tech in any discipline with minimum 60% marks. Candidates must have 60% aggregate in Class X and XII and minimum 60% marks in English in Class X or Class XII.
  • Naval Air Operations Officer (Observers): BE/B.Tech in any discipline with minimum 60% marks; 60% aggregate in Class X and XII and minimum 60% marks in English in Class X or Class XII.
  • Air Traffic Controller (ATC): Same as Pilot / Observers entry.
  • Logistics: (a) BE/B.Tech in any discipline with First Class; OR (b) MBA with First Class; OR (c) B.Sc/B.Com/B.Sc (IT) with First Class along with PG Diploma in Finance/Logistics/Supply Chain Management/Material Management; OR (d) MCA/M.Sc (IT) with First Class.
  • Naval Armament Inspectorate Cadre (NAIC): BE/B.Tech with minimum 60% marks in streams including Mechanical, Aeronautical, Electrical & Electronics, Electronics, Micro Electronics, Industrial Production, Instrumentation & Control, Electronics & Communication, Industrial Engineering, Aero Space, Control Engineering, Information Technology, Production, Instrumentation, Applied Electronics & Instrumentation, Electronics & Tele Communication, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Computer Application, Metallurgy, Metallurgical, Chemical, Material Science; OR Post Graduate degree in Electronics/Physics. Candidates must have 60% aggregate marks in Class X and XII and minimum 60% marks in English in Class X or Class XII.
  • Education: Multiple streams accepted including MSc/MA in Maths/Operational Research/Physics/Applied Physics/Meteorology/Oceanography/Atmospheric Sciences, MA (History) with min 55%, BE/B.Tech in Mechanical/Production/Electrical/Electronics/Communication/Electronics and Instrumentation, ME/M.Tech in Electronics/Communication/Controls/Radar/Microwave/Optical Fibre Communication/Digital Signal Processing/VLSI etc., ME/M.Tech in Thermal/Production/Machine Design/Mechatronics/Meteorology/Oceanography/Atmospheric Sciences (with Physics and Maths at graduation). Minimum 60% marks in Class X, XII, and minimum 60% marks in English in Class X or XII.
  • Engineering Branch (GS): BE/B.Tech with minimum 60% marks in Marine Engineering, Instrumentation Engineering, Production Engineering, Industrial Engineering & Management, Aero Space Engineering, Automobiles Engineering, Control Engineering, Instrumentation & Control, Metallurgy Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Mechanical/Mechanical with Automation.
  • Submarine Tech Engineering: Same as Engineering Branch (GS).
  • Electrical Branch (GS): BE/B.Tech with minimum 60% marks in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical & Electronics, Electronics & Tele Communication, Applied Electronics & Instrumentation, Instrumentation, Tele Communication, Electronics & Communication, Power Electronics, Power Engineering, Instrumentation & Control, Electronics & Instrumentation, Applied Electronics and Communication (AEC).
  • Submarine Tech Electrical: Same as Electrical Branch (GS).
  • Naval Constructor: BE/B.Tech with minimum 60% marks in Mechanical/Mechanical with Automation, Civil Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Aero Space Engineering, Marine Engineering, Ship Technology, Naval Architecture, Metallurgy, Ship Building, Ship Design, Ocean Engineering.

The Indian Navy officer age limit 2026 varies by branch. Refer to the vacancy table above for branch-specific date-of-birth ranges. All candidates must be unmarried at the time of applying. The selected candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant.

Who Can Apply?

  • Candidates who have obtained a graduate/post-graduate degree or are in the final year.
  • Degree must be from a university incorporated by an Act of Central or State Legislature in India, or other institutions established by Act of Parliament or deemed to be Universities/Autonomous Universities under UGC Act 1956, IIT Act 1961, AICTE Act 1987, NITSER Act 2007, IIT Act 2014.
  • Candidates studying in the possession of a degree from foreign institutions may also apply for any Branch/Cadre as enumerated above, with an equivalence certificate of the degree from UGC.

Indian Navy SSC Selection Process 2026

The Indian Navy SSC selection process 2026 is a multi-stage procedure that begins with shortlisting based on normalised marks and culminates in a merit list after SSB interview and medical examination. Understanding each stage will help candidates prepare strategically for this defence government job.

Stage 1 – Shortlisting for SSB Interview

Shortlisting will be done using formulae mentioned on the Indian Navy website (https://www.joinindiannavy.gov.in/files/normalisation.pdf). Marks obtained by candidates in the qualifying degree will be considered for SSB shortlisting.

  • BE/B.Tech candidates: Marks obtained up to the fifth semester will be considered. For candidates in the final year, shortlisting will be based on final-year performance.
  • Post-Graduate Degree Programme candidates: For those who have completed MSc, MCA, MBA, M.Tech, marks obtained in all semesters will be considered.

Stage 2 – SSB Interview

Shortlisted candidates will be informed about their selection for SSB interview through e-mail or SMS. Candidates are advised not to change their e-mail/mobile number till selection process is over and to check their inbox and spam folder periodically. Change of SSB Centre for interview is not permissible under any circumstances.

Stage 3 – Medical Examination

SSB-recommended candidates will be required to inform their final result of their respective degree to the Indian Navy at [email protected] prior to 20 June 2027. Candidates declared fit in the medical examination would be appointed as per availability of vacancies in the entry.

Stage 4 – Merit List

A merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks for all entries, after medical clearance for the respective entry. Mere inclusion in the select list does not confer a vested right to appointment. All vacancies are to be filled as per service requirement and as per statutory guidelines issued from time to time.

Indian Navy Officer Salary 2026

One of the most frequently searched topics for this recruitment is the Indian Navy officer salary 2026. Selected candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant. Here are the key pay and allowance details as mentioned in the official notification:

  • The initial gross salary of a Sub Lieutenant starts from Rs 1,20,000/- (approximately) per month, along with other allowances as applicable.
  • Pilot/NAOO and Submarine allowance of Rs 31,250/- will be admissible to candidates post successful completion of training.
  • Further details on pay, allowances, Group Insurance and Gratuity/Leave Entitlements/Duties of Officers are available on the Indian Navy website at www.joinindiannavy.gov.in.

Calculate your exact in-hand Salary in 10 seconds - Calculate Now

Tenure of Commission

Selected candidates will be granted Short Service Commission initially for 12 years, extendable by a maximum of 02 years, subject to service requirement, performance, medical eligibility, and willingness of candidates.

Indian Navy SSC Probation Period

Probation period for all branches/cadres is two years. The probation period will commence from the date of grant of the rank of Sub Lieutenant and will terminate after two years or on completion of initial training (whichever is later). During probation, officers are liable to be discharged in case of unsatisfactory performance at any stage.

Also read: SSC SSA/UDC LDCE 2025 Notification Out - Apply Online for 227 Group C Posts

Indian Navy Physical and Medical Standards 2026

Candidates are strongly advised to ascertain their eligibility for branches with respect to applicable medical standards, prior to indicating their preference. This is especially relevant for SSC (Pilot) entry where specified numbers of candidates based on service requirement will be considered for SSB/CPSS/Aviation Medical Examination.

  • A specified number of candidates for SSC (Pilot) entry will be considered for SSB/CPSS/Aviation Medical Examination and are advised to check physical/medical standards (Height, leg length etc.) before selecting this option.
  • Remaining candidates will be considered for other preferences opted by them.
  • Candidates declared medically fit for DG Jul 27 course will be considered fit for all SSC branches of IN (except for Pilot/NAOO).
  • Please visit www.joinindiannavy.gov.in for information. SSB-recommended candidates must undergo medical examination applicable to their entry. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.

Training Details – Indian Naval Academy

Candidates selected for the Indian Navy SSC Jun 2027 (AT 27) Course will undergo training at the Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala, Kerala. Key training-related points are as follows:

  • Candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant, subject to clearing induction medical examination at INA, Ezhimala upon posting.
  • Only unmarried candidates are eligible for training. Any candidate found to be married or who marries during training will be discharged from service.
  • Candidates must fulfil the educational qualification stipulated above before joining INA, Ezhimala by June 2027. The candidate failing to meet stipulated educational criteria will not be permitted to join INA, Ezhimala.
  • Male candidates shortlisted for GS(X) are also eligible to volunteer for submarine arm subject to medical fitness, vacancies, and service requirements.

Apply Online – Indian Navy SSC Officer 2026

Candidates who meet the Indian Navy SSC eligibility criteria 2026 can apply online through the official Indian Navy recruitment portal. The online application process is active from 25 June 2026 and the final deadline is 27 July 2026. No applications will be accepted after the last date.

Important instructions before applying:

  • Candidates must register and fill the application on the Indian Navy website at www.joinindiannavy.gov.in. To save time, candidates can fill in their details and upload documents in advance.
  • Whilst filling the e-application, keep the following documents readily available:
    • Correct personal particulars (as given in Matriculation Certificate)
    • Valid e-mail address and mobile number (mandatory fields)
    • CGPA covering up to 5th & 7th semester for regular and integrated BE/B.Tech courses respectively and all semesters for other degree programmes
    • All relevant documents (preferably mark sheets up to 10th & 12th certificate)
    • Date of birth proof (as proof of 10th or 12th certificate)
    • NCC 'C' certificate issued by National Cadet Corps (if applicable)
    • Recent passport-size colour photograph in original JPG/TIFF format
  • If any scanned document is not legible/readable, the application will be rejected. Candidates must take a printout of the application and carry it while appearing for SSB interview.
  • The application once submitted will be final and no request for amendments/change will be entertained.
  • Multiple applications for this course by any candidate will lead to cancellation of his/her candidature.

Indian Navy SSC Officer 2026 Apply Online Link: Apply Here

Common Application Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates make avoidable errors while applying for defence jobs in India 2026. Based on general guidance for government online application processes, here are common mistakes to be careful about:

  • Uploading blurred, low-resolution, or incorrectly formatted photographs and documents - these lead to rejection.
  • Entering incorrect personal details that do not match your Matriculation Certificate.
  • Selecting a branch for which you do not meet the educational qualification or stream requirement.
  • Failing to include CGPA/marks for all required semesters as specified for your course type.
  • Changing your registered mobile number or e-mail address after submission - you may miss SSB shortlisting communications.
  • Submitting multiple application forms - this will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Not taking a printout of the submitted application - candidates must carry it to the SSB interview.

How to Check Your RBI Grade B DEPR Phase-I Result

This section explains the exact process for confirming your roll number in the official result document, so you know where to look and what to avoid.

The result has been published as a roll-number list within an official PDF on the RBI website. Rather than depending on third-party lists, always verify your own status directly.

  • Visit the official RBI website: www.rbi.org.in, or the Opportunities@RBI recruitment portal.
  • Open the official Phase-I DEPR Result PDF for the roll number list.
  • Use Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F) on the PDF and search for your own roll number.
  • Save or download the PDF for your future reference.

RBI has also noted a standard disclaimer with this result: despite careful preparation, the Board reserves the right to correct any inadvertent errors. If you spot a discrepancy in your details, wait for an official corrigendum rather than relying on unverified sources.

Candidates applying for the DEPR cadre must possess a Master's Degree in Economics, or a Master's Degree in Finance/PGDM/MBA from a recognized university or institution.

RBI Grade B DEPR Phase-II Exam 2026: Key Details

This section explains what to expect in the Phase-II stage, including the exam date, shift structure, and admit card rules points candidates often get confused about.

Phase-II for the DEPR cadre is scheduled for July 26, 2026, and will be conducted in two shifts on the same day. A few important points to note:

  • One exam, two shifts: Candidates must appear for all papers across both shifts attending only one shift is not allowed.
  • Single admit card: RBI will issue only one admit card covering both shifts, unlike exams that issue separate call letters per shift.
  • No logistical flexibility: No request for change of exam date, shift, centre, or venue will be entertained under any circumstance. Plan your travel and stay in advance once your centre is confirmed.

How to Download the RBI Grade B Phase-II Admit Card

This section provides the step-by-step process to download your Phase-II admit card once RBI activates the link.

  1. Visit the official RBI website: www.rbi.org.in.
  2. Locate the Phase-II admit card link under the careers/recruitment section.
  3. Log in using your registration number and password/date of birth.
  4. Download the admit card and verify your exam date, shift timing, and venue carefully.
  5. Along with the admit card, RBI will also release an Information Handout for Phase-II, plus separate instructions for PwBD candidates using a scribe or compensatory time, and for candidates with specified disability (less than 40%) who have difficulty writing.

This section explains the overall stages of selection for the Officer Grade B recruitment, as outlined in the official notification.

According to the official recruitment details, the selection process comprises:

  • Online Examination (CBT) Phase-I and Phase-II

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) released the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 on 30th June 2026 for candidates who appeared in the CRP RRBs-XIV recruitment cycle. Candidates who were not allotted a bank in the main result can now log in to the official IBPS portal with their registration number and password/date of birth to check their provisional allotment status under the reserve list. What Is the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026?

This section explains the purpose of the reserve list and why IBPS issues it after the main selection round.

A reserve list is a backup panel that IBPS prepares after declaring the final result of the CRP RRBs-XIV exam. Once the primary list of selected candidates is allotted to participating banks, some vacancies remain unfilled because certain selected candidates do not join within the deadline, resign shortly after joining, or get rejected at the document verification stage. To ensure every sanctioned post is filled, IBPS draws candidates from the reserve panel, based on merit, category, and the number of vacancies still open, and provisionally allots them to a Regional Rural Bank for the Office Assistant/Customer Service Associate (Clerk) post.

How to Check IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 Online?

This section outlines the step-by-step process to view and download your reserve list allotment status.

  1. Visit the official IBPS website at ibps.in.
  2. Click on the "CRP-CSA (Customer Service Associate)" tab on the homepage.
  3. Select "CRP-CRP XIV – Provisional Allotment under Reserve List."
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code and click on the Login button.
  6. View your allotment status and download the result for future reference.

How Will You Know If You're Selected?

This section explains how IBPS notifies candidates who get provisional allotment through the reserve list.

Candidates who are provisionally allotted a bank through the reserve list will receive an official communication via email and SMS on their registered email ID and mobile number. It is advisable to regularly check your registered contact details and the official IBPS portal so you don't miss any update.

What Happens After the Reserve List Allotment?

This section explains the next stages candidates must complete after receiving a provisional allotment.

Getting your name on the reserve list does not mean final selection it is a provisional allotment that becomes confirmed only after the bank completes verification. The typical process that follows includes:

  • Document Verification: Submission of original certificates and identity proofs for cross-checking.
  • Submission of Required Certificates: Educational, category, and other eligibility-related documents as specified by the allotted bank.
  • Medical Examination: Some banks may require a fitness check before final confirmation.
  • Joining Formalities: Completion of paperwork and reporting to the allotted branch.
  • Induction/Training Process: Orientation and training conducted by the bank before you begin regular duties.

Candidates should keep all original and photocopied documents ready in advance to avoid last-minute issues during verification.

Why Does IBPS Release a Reserve List?

This section explains the broader purpose behind the reserve list mechanism in IBPS recruitment.

A reserve list helps maintain smooth recruitment by ensuring sanctioned vacancies don't remain vacant. It benefits candidates who narrowly missed the initial cut-off by giving them another opportunity, while also helping banks manage manpower requirements efficiently across states and categories.

Eligibility Criteria for MSC Bank Cooperative Intern 2026

To be eligible for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026, candidates must have completed a full 2-year MBA or PGDM in specific management disciplines from an AICTE/UGC-accredited institution. Candidates who are currently pursuing their MBA or PGDM course and have not yet completed it are not eligible to apply. Additionally, computer proficiency is listed as an essential qualification alongside the management degree.

Educational Qualification

MBA or 2-year Post Graduate Diploma in Management (PGDM) in any of the following specialisations, from an institution accredited by AICTE or UGC:

  • Marketing Management
  • Cooperative Management
  • Agri Business Management
  • Rural Development Management

Only candidates who have successfully completed the 2-year MBA/PGDM course are eligible. Those currently pursuing the course cannot apply.

Roles and Responsibilities of Cooperative Intern

Candidates applying for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Programme 2026 will be assigned substantive responsibilities at the grassroots level. The intern is not merely an observer - they are expected to coordinate with Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and other primary cooperatives, and prepare weekly progress reports for the Ministry of Cooperation. This is a full-time programme, and interns must observe the working hours of the concerned bank.

Key duties include:

  • Coordinating with Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) and other primary cooperatives to provide guidance for implementing Ministry of Cooperation initiatives
  • Solving day-to-day problems faced by PACS in computerisation, preparation of business plans, projects, financing issues, and various approvals
  • Preparing and sharing weekly status reports on the implementation of Ministry of Cooperation initiatives, in coordination with the State Cooperative Bank and District Central Cooperative Banks

Selection Process - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026

The selection process for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026 is straightforward - applications are accepted offline, and only shortlisted candidates will be called for an interview. Final selection is at the discretionary power of the Bank/Selection Committee. There is no written examination mentioned in the notification.

Step 1 - Application Screening: The bank shortlists candidates from the offline applications received based on eligibility criteria.

Step 2 - Interview: Only shortlisted candidates are called for a personal interview. The exact date and venue of the interview are communicated to shortlisted candidates directly.

Step 3 - Final Selection: The Selection Committee's decision on final selection is discretionary and binding.

How to Apply Offline - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Apply 2026

The MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Apply 2026 process is entirely offline - there is no online application portal for this recruitment. Candidates must download the prescribed application form (Annexure-I) from the bank's website, fill it in their own handwriting, attach all supporting documents, and physically submit it to the bank's Mumbai head office before the deadline. Applications submitted after 5:15 PM on 10 July 2026 will not be accepted.

Step-by-step application process:

  1. Visit the official MSC Bank website at https://msc.bank.in/career and download the Application Form (Annexure-I)
  2. Fill the application form in your own handwriting with all required details including name, address, date of birth, educational qualifications, MBA/PGDM specialisation, computer proficiency, work experience, and references
  3. Affix a recent passport-size photograph in the designated space and sign in the signature box
  4. Attach self-attested photocopies of all relevant qualification certificates, computer proficiency certificate, and experience certificates (if any)
  5. Provide details of two references - bankers, professionals, or government officials who are residents of India, holders of responsible positions, and not related to you
  6. Place the completed application and all documents in a sealed envelope
  7. Write "Application for the post of Cooperative Intern" on the envelope
  8. Submit or send the sealed envelope to:
    The Joint Manager (OSD), HRD&M Department, The Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank Ltd., Sir Vithaldas Thackersey Memorial Building, 9, Maharashtra Chamber of Commerce Lane, Fort, Mumbai – 400001
  9. Ensure delivery on or before 10 July 2026 till 5:15 PM

Documents Required - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern 2026

Candidates must enclose self-attested photocopies of all supporting documents along with the application form (Annexure-I). Submitting incorrect or false information makes the candidate liable for disqualification and, if appointed, for dismissal from service without notice.

Required documents to enclose with the application:

  • Passport-size photograph (affixed on the form)
  • Proof of date of birth

Important Terms and Conditions for MSC Bank Cooperative Interns

Candidates must clearly understand that the MSC Bank Cooperative Internship 2026 is not a job offer and does not create any right or claim for regular employment with MSC Bank or any associated institution. The internship can be discontinued at any time without payment of financial benefit if the intern's performance is unsatisfactory or if the intern is absent without authorisation. Interns are also bound by strict confidentiality obligations regarding bank documents, policies, and business plans.

Key terms to note:

  • This is a full-time internship programme - interns must observe bank working hours
  • The internship may be terminated at any time without assigning reasons
  • Interns must not interact with media (print/electronic/social media) or represent the bank without express permission
  • Interns must maintain confidentiality of all documents, reports, and information received during the internship - violation entails legal consequences
  • No intern can post work-related content on social media without written permission from competent authority
  • The internship confers no right to employment with the bank or associated institutions

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Since the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern application process is entirely offline, several common errors can lead to rejection. Being aware of these before submitting your application saves time and avoids disappointment.

  • Applying while still pursuing MBA/PGDM: The notification is clear - candidates currently pursuing the 2-year MBA/PGDM are not eligible. Only those who have already completed the degree should apply.
  • Missing the 5:15 PM deadline on 10 July 2026: This is not a midnight deadline - it is 5:15 PM sharp. Applications received even minutes after 5:15 PM on 10 July will not be accepted. Plan for early submission or courier delivery with tracking.
  • Not filling the form in own handwriting: The application form (Annexure-I) must be handwritten by the candidate. Typed or printed personal details in the form may be grounds for rejection.
  • Not mentioning MBA/PGDM specialisation clearly: The form has a checkbox for specialisation (Marketing Management, Cooperative Management, Agri Business Management, Rural Development Management). Leaving this blank creates ambiguity.
  • Omitting computer proficiency certificate: Computer proficiency is listed as an essential qualification. Candidates who do not enclose proof of MS-CIT or equivalent certification risk rejection.
  • Providing relatives as references: The notification explicitly states that references must not be relations. Providing a family member as a reference is a disqualifying error.
  • Wrong envelope superscription: The envelope must be labelled "Application for the post of Cooperative Intern." Using any other labelling or no labelling may result in the envelope being misrouted.
  • Submitting only the form without supporting documents: Self-attested photocopies of all qualification certificates must accompany the form. An incomplete application without supporting documents will not be processed.

What Is the RBI Young Professional Programme?

The RBI Young Professional programme is a unique initiative by the Reserve Bank of India designed to bring domain specialists into the central bank's functioning on a contractual basis. Unlike recruitment for regular officer grades, this programme targets individuals with specialized postgraduate or technical expertise who can contribute meaningfully to short-to-medium-term policy-related research and analytical assignments.

Selected Young Professionals work within RBI's Central Office Departments in Mumbai, gaining direct exposure to India's most consequential financial, monetary, and regulatory policy decisions. The engagement enriches both the Bank's analytical capacity and the professional development of selected candidates. It is not a pathway to permanent employment at RBI, but it is widely regarded as an extraordinary professional experience within India's financial policy ecosystem.

Post-wise Eligibility and Job Profiles: Complete Breakdown

Every RBI Young Professional post has its own educational qualification requirements, desirable experience profile, and distinct job profile. Understanding these differences is critical before applying - using the wrong post code in your email subject line can result in rejection.

1. YP0626DOS01 - Cyber Security and Information Technology Risk

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This role is designed for specialists who can help RBI assess technology risks, digital resilience, and cybersecurity threats across the regulated financial sector.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree or equivalent in Cyber Security / Information Security / Computer Science / IT / Data Science / AI or a related field.
  • Desirable Qualifications & Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CEH, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, AWS/Azure Security; published research in IT, Cybersecurity, or Public Policy journals.

Desirable Experience:

  • Cyber security, technology risk management, digital regulation, or fintech
  • Cloud security, cyber resilience, digital transformation projects
  • Experience with financial institutions, regulators, CERTs, or tech companies

What You Will Do: Conduct policy research on cyber security and digital resilience; draft framework documents; analyze cyber incidents and threat intelligence trends; support AI/ML, cloud security, and data governance projects.

2. YP0626DOS02 - Policy Analytics (DoS)

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This data-heavy role requires candidates who can transform complex supervisory data into actionable analytical outputs using advanced tools.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Computer Science/IT, or Master's degree in Statistics/Data Science.

Desirable Technical Skills:

  • Excel (Power Query, Power Pivot, VBA macros, automation)
  • Power BI (Advanced DAX, interactive dashboards, drill-through functionality)
  • Python (Pandas, NumPy, ETL workflows, automated reporting)
  • Statistics (regression analysis, forecasting, hypothesis testing, predictive modelling)
  • MIS Automation and large multi-source data management

What You Will Do: Extract and analyze supervisory datasets; develop Power BI dashboards; automate recurring MIS reports using VBA and Python; prepare analytical notes and policy briefs for senior management; support RTI/legal matters through structured data review.

3. YP0626DOR01 - Climate Change Risk and Sustainable Finance

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

With climate-related financial risks gaining regulatory prominence worldwide, this role positions the selected candidate at the frontier of ESG and sustainable finance regulation in India.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or PG qualification in Climate Change Studies / Environmental Science / Environmental Management / Climate Finance / Sustainability / Economics / Financial Economics / Finance / Statistics / Econometrics / Data Science / Public Policy / Disaster Management / Natural Resource Management / related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Certifications: FRM (GARP), SCR (GARP), ESG-related certifications.
  • Desirable Skills: Knowledge of physical and transition climate risks; understanding of ESG frameworks; Python, R, SQL, Excel, or data visualization tools.
  • What You Will Do: Climate risk research and analysis; policy support and regulatory framework development; climate stress testing; ESG and sustainable finance work; preparation of reports and policy notes; stakeholder engagement and capacity building.

4. YP0626DOR02 - Credit Risk Analytics & Regulatory Policy

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

This post is aimed at quantitatively strong candidates who can contribute to credit risk regulation, macroprudential analysis, and evidence-based policy development.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or equivalent in Economics / Econometrics / Statistics / Finance / Mathematics / Data Science / Financial Engineering or related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Qualification: PhD in Finance, Economics, or Statistics; or published research in credit risk or financial stability.
  • Desirable Experience: Risk modelling in financial institutions or credit rating agencies; experience with Python and large datasets; familiarity with ECL/IFRS-9, credit bureau data, BCBS and FSB regulatory standards.
  • What You Will Do: Frame and review credit risk regulations; identify regulatory gaps; support evidence-based policy; analyze international regulatory developments; develop analytical frameworks for assessing the impact of regulatory policies.

5. YP0626DPS01 - Payment Ecosystem

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This role calls for candidates who can track and analyze developments in India's rapidly evolving payment ecosystem, including cross-border payment architectures.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Payment systems, cross-border payments, public policy, or financial markets.

What You Will Do: Monitor market intelligence from international bodies (CPMI, FATF, BIS); undertake primary and secondary research on global payment architectures; generate analytical reports for international forums; statistical modelling of payment flow data.

6. YP0626DPS02 - Policy and Research in Domestic & Cross-Border Payment Systems

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This position supports RBI's top management with policy notes, research briefs, and market intelligence covering both domestic and international payment developments.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Public policy, payment systems.

What You Will Do: Prepare notes and briefs for RBI's top management on payment system policy; track domestic and international payment ecosystem developments; gather market intelligence from CPMI, FATF, BIS; contribute to research and thematic studies on payment systems.

7. YP0626DEP01 - Policy and Research (DEPR)

Department: Department of Economic and Policy Research, Central Office, Mumbai

This is one of the most academically demanding posts in the RBI YP 2026 recruitment, designed for candidates with strong economics research credentials.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's or PhD in Economics, with at least one course paper in Mathematics, Statistics, or Econometrics during the Master's programme.
  • Desirable Qualification: Authored at least one paper in a reputed journal ranked B or above.
  • Desirable Experience: Economic research; experience with STATA, EViews, Python, or R.
  • What You Will Do: Review research papers and reports on policy and regulatory matters; prepare concise summaries and background notes for RBI's top management; support senior leadership in meetings and presentations.

8. YP0626FIN01 - Artificial Intelligence

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

As AI transforms the financial sector, RBI seeks a specialist who can shape its approach to AI governance, ethics, and regulatory oversight.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in AI / Computer Science / Public Policy / Data Science or a related discipline.
  • Desirable Knowledge: AI governance, machine learning concepts, data ethics, emerging technology policy frameworks.
  • Desirable Experience: AI research, technology policy, data analysis; exposure to ethical AI frameworks, regulatory research, or public policy projects.
  • What You Will Do: Analyse emerging AI technologies; develop policy recommendations on ethics, governance, data privacy, and responsible AI adoption; support regulatory research and stakeholder consultations; assist in strategy formulation for AI-driven innovation ecosystems.

9. YP0626FIN02 - Quantum Technology

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This highly specialized and forward-looking role places a candidate at the cutting edge of India's quantum technology policy landscape.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in Quantum Computing / Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / Technology Policy.
  • Desirable Knowledge: Quantum technologies, cybersecurity implications, innovation policy research.
  • Desirable Experience: Quantum technology research, emerging technology analysis, quantum computing applications, or cybersecurity research.
  • What You Will Do: Conduct research on quantum computing, communication, and cybersecurity trends; assist in developing strategic frameworks for quantum ecosystem development; support standards-setting and international collaboration initiatives.

10. YP0626FMO01 - Data Analysis

Department: Financial Markets Operations Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role suits a candidate who can translate financial market data into policy-relevant insights, particularly in the money market domain.

  • Essential Qualification: Post Graduation in Statistics / Economics with Econometrics as a subject.
  • Desirable Qualifications: CFA, FRM; proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
  • Desirable Experience: Econometrics; published research; banking dealer experience; money market exposure.
  • What You Will Do: Perform data analysis to support policy research; track domestic and global currency and yield movements; analyze money market rates on a daily basis.

11. YP0626FMR01 - Financial Markets

Department: Financial Markets Regulation Department, Central Office, Mumbai

A role for quantitatively oriented professionals who can harness analytical tools to study and interpret financial market behavior for regulatory purposes.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree in Economics / Operations Research / Finance / Statistics / Mathematics.
  • Desirable Experience: Any area related to financial markets.
  • What You Will Do: Study and analyze financial market data using cutting-edge analytical tools in close coordination with the regulatory function.

12. YP0626CEP01 - Data Analytics and Policy Research

Department: Consumer Education and Protection Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role focuses on using data science and machine learning to understand consumer complaint trends and translate them into policy inputs for RBI's leadership.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech, or Postgraduate degree in Mathematics / Statistics / Computer Science / Economics / Data Analytics with knowledge of statistical tools and Power BI.
  • Desirable Skills: Python, R, or SQL for automation, machine learning, and large dataset handling.
  • What You Will Do: Data mining and analytics using AI/ML tools; systematic classification of consumer complaints and trends; process automation of report generation; development of interactive real-time dashboards; preparation of quality policy inputs for RBI's top management.

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the following baseline conditions to be considered for any of the 12 Young Professional positions at RBI. These are non-negotiable and checked at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age Limit: Must be above 21 years and not more than 30 years of age as on July 6, 2026. The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories under this recruitment.
  • Educational Qualification: Must meet the post-specific eligibility criteria as detailed in Annexure-III of the official notification. All qualifications must be from a recognized institution in India or abroad. In cases of similar or alternative qualifications, RBI retains sole authority to determine equivalency.
  • Agreement to Terms: Candidates must agree to the Terms and Conditions of Engagement as specified in the notification.
  • Application Mode: Must apply via email in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-VI of the official notification).

Each post has its own essential qualification. Meeting the general age criterion alone does not guarantee eligibility - always check the post-specific educational requirement before applying.

Monthly Stipend and Terms of Engagement

Understanding what this role offers - and what it does not - is essential before applying. RBI's YP engagement is a contractual position with a generous stipend but with clearly defined boundaries.

Remuneration

A fixed monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000 will be paid throughout the engagement period, subject to applicable tax deductions. No additional allowances, HRA, or benefits are provided over and above this stipend.

Contract Duration

The initial contract tenure is 3 years, which may be extended by mutual agreement for a total period not exceeding 5 years. The extension decision is based solely on the Bank's assessment of the YP's performance and is at RBI's discretion.

Nature of Engagement

This is a contractual, full-time engagement - not a regular or permanent appointment. The YP will have no claim to any regular or permanent position at RBI by virtue of this engagement. There is no employer-employee relationship between RBI and the YP.

Leave Policy

YPs are entitled to 15 days of leave per calendar year, accrued on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Leave cannot be carried forward to the next year. Absence beyond this entitlement is treated as leave without pay, with a proportionate deduction from the monthly stipend. Unauthorized absence for 8 or more consecutive working days without valid reason may lead to contract termination.

Termination and Notice Period

Either party may terminate the contract with 3 months' notice. However, during the first 6 months of the initial tenure, the contract may be terminated by either side without any notice period.

Other Conditions

  • Place of engagement is Mumbai; no residential accommodation will be provided by RBI
  • No part-time work for any private or public body is permitted during the engagement without prior written permission from RBI
  • YPs must produce a medical fitness certificate and a satisfactory police verification report on selection
  • A code of conduct agreement and secrecy undertaking must be signed on joining
  • In the event of death, injury, or illness during tenure, neither the YP nor their dependents are entitled to compensation or employment from RBI

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Apply Link & Process

The application process for RBI YP 2026 is entirely email-based. There is no online portal, no registration system, and no walk-in interview. Every step must be followed precisely to avoid rejection.

Step 1 - Download the Application Proforma: Download Annexure-VI from the official notification document available at www.rbi.org.in. Fill it out completely. Fields marked with asterisk (*) are mandatory.

Step 2 - Prepare Your Documents: Compile all the following in PDF format:

  • Duly filled application proforma (Annexure-VI) with recent colour photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Degree certificates for essential and desirable qualifications (provisional certificate acceptable if the degree is pending)
  • Statement of Interest (explaining why you are applying for the specific post)
  • A sample of academic or policy writing
  • A reference/recommendation letter from a professional referee (preferably from your current/previous employer or academic institution)

Step 3 - Check the Email Specifications:

  • All documents must be in PDF format only - other formats may be blocked by RBI's security filters
  • Total attachment size must not exceed 5 MB
  • The email body must be concise (one or two lines) and unconditional - no additional statements

Step 4 - Format the Email Subject Line Correctly:
The subject line must follow this exact format: "YP Application - [Post Code] - [Your Full Name]"
Example: YP Application - YP0626FIN01 - Ramesh Kumar

Step 5 - Send the Application:
Email your complete application to [email protected] before the deadline.

Step 6 - Applying for Multiple Posts:
If you wish to apply for more than one position, send a separate email for each post. Each email must include a complete, independent set of all required documents.

Selection Process for RBI YP 2026

Submitting a complete and eligible application is only the first step. The selection process for RBI Young Professionals involves multiple stages, and meeting the minimum eligibility is not a guarantee of progression.

Stage 1 - Preliminary Screening: A screening committee reviews all received applications against the eligibility criteria and the quality of supporting documents. The Bank reserves the right to limit the number of candidates called for interview.

Stage 2 - Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates will be required to submit and verify original documents related to age, educational qualifications, and experience.

Stage 3 - Interview: Shortlisted candidates will receive an interview call letter via email only. No physical call letters will be sent by post. Candidates must make their own travel and accommodation arrangements for the interview.

Reserve List: RBI maintains a reserve list of suitable candidates, valid for one year from the date of publication of the selection list.

RBI's decision regarding shortlisting, interview, and all aspects of engagement is final. No correspondence will be entertained in this regard.

Final-year or final-semester students can also apply provisionally, but they must produce proof of having passed the graduation examination on or before 30 September 2026 if shortlisted for interview. Candidates holding professional qualifications such as Medical, Engineering, Chartered Accountancy, or Cost Accountancy, as well as those with an Integrated Dual Degree (IDD) passed by the cut-off date, are also eligible.

Number of Attempts Allowed in SBI PO Exam

SBI has fixed a maximum number of attempts permissible for this exam based on category, and candidates who have already exhausted their permissible chances are not eligible to apply again. Appearing in the Main Examination counts as one attempt, while appearing only in the Preliminary Examination does not count as an attempt.

Category Maximum Permissible Chances
UR / EWS 6
UR (PwBD) / EWS (PwBD) / OBC / OBC (PwBD) 9
SC / SC (PwBD) / ST / ST (PwBD) No Restriction

SBI PO Application Fee 2026

The application fee for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 is Rs 750 for Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates, while SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted from paying any fee. This fee is non-refundable once paid and cannot be carried forward or held in reserve for any other examination, so candidates should confirm their category and details before making the payment.

SBI PO Previous Year Question Papers: Download PDF Here

CIBIL Score Requirement for SBI PO Candidates

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment relates to credit history, since SBI PO is a banking role with financial responsibility. Candidates who have defaulted on repayment under any loan, NBFC, or financial institution arrangement, including credit card dues, and whose accounts reflect adverse credit history in CIBIL or another recognised credit agency, must regularise or repay all outstanding dues on or before the date of joining the Bank. If the adverse status has not been updated in CIBIL records by the joining date, candidates must either get the status updated or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the lender confirming there are no outstanding dues; failure to do so will render the candidate ineligible and the offer of appointment will be withdrawn. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying.

SBI PO Selection Process 2026: Prelims, Mains & Interview

Selection for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 follows a three-phase process: Phase-I Preliminary Examination, Phase-II Main Examination, and Phase-III Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview. Candidates must clear each phase to be considered for the next, and only the marks from Phase-II and Phase-III are carried forward to prepare the final merit list.

Phase-I: SBI PO Prelims Exam Pattern 2026

The Preliminary Examination is an online objective test carrying 100 marks, to be completed in 1 hour, with separate timing for each of its three sections. There is no sectional cut-off in the Preliminary Exam, but a category-wise merit list is prepared based on the aggregate score, and candidates numbering approximately 10 times the vacancies in each category are shortlisted for the Main Exam.

Section No. of Questions Marks Duration
English Language 40 - 20 minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 - 20 minutes
Reasoning Ability 30 - 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 hour

Phase-II: SBI PO Mains Exam Pattern 2026

The Main Examination is conducted online and consists of an Objective Test of 200 marks and a Descriptive Test of 30 marks, taken together in 3 hours 30 minutes. The descriptive paper is administered immediately after the objective test, and candidates must type their answers directly on the computer.

Section No. of Questions Max Marks Duration
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 40 60 50 minutes
Data Analysis & Interpretation 30 60 45 minutes
General Awareness / Economy / Banking Knowledge 60 60 45 minutes
English Language 40 20 40 minutes
Objective Test Total 170 200 3 hours
Descriptive Test (Email / Situation Analysis / Report or Precis Writing) 3 30 30 minutes
Grand Total 230 3 hours 30 minutes  

Each candidate must score a minimum qualifying mark in every individual section, including the descriptive paper, with sectional cut-offs decided by the Bank based on vacancies. A category-wise merit list is then prepared from the aggregate Main Exam score, and candidates numbering approximately 3 times the category-wise vacancies are shortlisted for Phase-III.

There is also a penalty for wrong answers in both the Preliminary and Main objective tests: for every wrong answer, 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question is deducted, while unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Phase-III: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview

Shortlisted candidates undergo a Psychometric Test for personality profiling, followed by a Group Exercise (20 marks) and a Personal Interview (30 marks), totalling 50 marks. The Psychometric Test findings are shared with the interview panel to give a fuller perspective on each candidate, and all questions in this test are mandatory.

Final Merit List and Normalisation

The marks from Phase-II (Main Exam, both Objective and Descriptive) and Phase-III (Group Exercise & Interview) are normalised to 100 marks each before being combined into the final merit list; marks from the Preliminary Exam are not added at this stage.

Component Maximum Marks Normalised Marks
Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) 230 75
Group Exercise & Interview 50 25
Total 280 100

If two or more candidates score identical marks at the cut-off point in the final merit list, they are ranked according to age in descending order, meaning the older candidate is placed higher.

SBI PO Apply Online 2026: Step-by-Step Registration Guide

Candidates can apply for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 only in online mode, from 18 June 2026 to 8 July 2026; no other mode of application is accepted. Before starting, candidates must have a valid personal email ID and mobile number kept active until the declaration of the final result, since all call letters and result-related communication will be sent there.

  1. Visit SBI's official careers portal at https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings (also accessible at https://bank.sbi/web/careers/current-openings) and locate Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09.
  2. Download and carefully read the detailed advertisement PDF before proceeding with registration.
  3. Click Apply Online and open the registration form under "Current Openings."
  4. Keep scanned images ready in advance: your photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, 200×230 pixels, 20–50 KB), signature (140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB), left-hand thumb impression (3cm x 3cm, 240×240 pixels, 20–50 KB), and a hand-written declaration (10cm x 5cm, 800×400 pixels, 50–100 KB), all in JPG/JPEG format.
  5. Fill in the application form carefully; you can save a partially completed form, which generates a provisional registration number and password that you must note down to resume later.
  6. Capture a live photograph through your webcam or mobile phone during registration, as this is mandatory in addition to the uploaded photograph.
  7. Recheck every field for accuracy, since no edits are allowed once the form is finally submitted.
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI; SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempt from the fee.
  9. On successful payment, download and print the e-receipt and application form for your records.
  10. Complete your application well before 8 July 2026 to avoid last-minute technical issues caused by heavy website traffic.

You can also apply directly through the dedicated SBI PO registration link at https://ibpsreg.ibps.in/sbipojun26/.

SBI PO Salary 2026: Pay Scale and CTC

Selected candidates for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 will draw a starting basic pay of Rs 48,480, plus 4 advance increments, in the Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I) pay scale of 48480-2000/7-62480-2340/2-67160-2680/7-85920. In addition to basic pay, officers are eligible for Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), City Compensatory Allowance (CCA), Provident Fund, the National Pension System (NPS), Leave Fare Concession (LFC), medical facilities, lease rental facility, and other allowances as per the Bank's prevailing rules. The approximate CTC at the initial pay scale for the Mumbai Centre works out to Rs 21.97 Lacs.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Joining, Bond and Probation Period

Selected candidates must complete a basic banking knowledge online course before joining and will be designated as Probationary Officers, placed on probation for two years with continuous performance assessment. At the time of joining, candidates must execute a bond of Rs 2.00 Lacs, committing to serve the Bank for a minimum period of three years; this bond is invoked if the candidate resigns before completing three years of service. Officers who clear the probation assessment standards are confirmed in JMGS-I, and SBI's promotion policy offers a path for high-performing officers to reach senior and top management grades, including opportunities for international postings.

SBI PO Exam Preparation 2026: Strategy, Exam Pattern, Selection Process & Study Plan

Documents and Identity Proof Required at Examination

Candidates must carry specific documents at each stage of the selection process, and missing or mismatched documents can lead to disqualification. At the time of the Preliminary and Main Examinations, candidates must bring a valid photo identity proof such as a Passport, Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Driving Licence, Voter's ID Card, or Bank Passbook with an attested photograph, along with a self-attested photocopy. The notification also specifies that candidates must possess a valid Aadhaar card, as SBI conducts online Aadhaar verification at different stages of the selection process, and biometric verification (photo and thumb impression/IRIS scan) may also be carried out.

For the Main Exam specifically, candidates must bring the duly authenticated Original Preliminary Exam Call Letter along with the authenticated ID proof copy, the Main Exam Call Letter, and two additional photographs identical to the one used during registration; candidates without these will not be allowed to appear. Use of mobile phones or any electronic devices inside the examination or interview premises is strictly banned and can lead to disqualification.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for SBI PO 2026

Many otherwise eligible candidates lose out due to small, avoidable errors during the application process, so it helps to be deliberate at each step. Keep your photograph, signature, thumb impression, and hand-written declaration within the exact pixel dimensions and file-size ranges specified, since uploads outside these limits will trigger an error and block submission; also remember that signatures and the hand-written declaration in capital letters are not accepted.

Avoid waiting until the closing date of 8 July 2026 to register, as heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions, and SBI does not take responsibility for applications that fail to go through for this reason. Double-check your category selection before final submission, since no change of category is permitted at any stage after registration, and incorrectly chosen reserved or unreserved status cannot be corrected later. If an online payment fails or appears incomplete, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the transaction went through, since the fee is strictly non-refundable. Finally, save your provisional registration number and password immediately after saving your form, and keep multiple copies of your registration photograph ready, as these are needed at every subsequent stage of the selection process.

What Is the RRB Group D Cut Off?

Before checking the numbers, it helps to understand what this cut off actually represents and why it differs across regions and categories.

The RRB Group D Cut Off is the minimum score a candidate must secure in the Computer Based Test (CBT) to qualify for the next stage of selection the Physical Efficiency Test (PET). It is not a fixed number; it is decided by each Railway Recruitment Board zone based on the number of vacancies in that zone, the difficulty level of the exam, and how candidates performed overall. Because RRB conducts the exam across multiple shifts and days, scores are normalized before the final cut off is calculated, ensuring fairness across different sets of question papers.

Factors Affecting RRB Group D Cut Off 2026

Cut off marks change every recruitment cycle. This section explains the main reasons why the 2026 cut off differs from previous years and across zones.

  • Number of vacancies: More vacancies in a zone generally lead to a lower cut off, while fewer vacancies push competition and the cut off higher.
  • Number of candidates appearing: Zones with a larger applicant pool tend to see a tougher, higher cut off.
  • Difficulty level of the exam: Easier shifts result in higher scores overall, which raises the cut off; tougher shifts have the opposite effect.
  • Zone-wise competition: Cut off marks vary from zone to zone since each RRB region has its own applicant base and vacancy count.
  • Category-wise reservation: Separate cut offs are released for UR, EWS, OBC, SC, and ST as per the reservation policy.
  • Score normalization: Since the CBT runs across multiple shifts and days, RRB normalizes scores to keep the process fair before deciding the final cut off.
  • Previous year's trends: Historical cut off data gives a reference point, though the final number always depends on the current cycle's specific vacancy and performance data.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective RRB zone (for example, rrbcdg.gov.in) or the unified portal rrb.indianrailways.gov.in.
  2. Look for the "RRB Group D CEN 08/2024 Result/Cut Off" notification link.
  3. Click to open the cut off PDF.
  4. Check the category-wise and zone-wise marks listed in the PDF.
  5. Download or save the PDF for future reference.

What's Next After the RRB Group D 2026 Cut Off?

Clearing the cut off is not the final step in selection. This section explains what happens after the CBT result and cut off are declared.

Candidates who score equal to or above the official cut off are shortlisted for the following stages:

  1. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) - A qualifying-only stage; marks scored here are not added to the final merit list.
  2. Document Verification (DV) - Verification of educational, category, and identity documents.
  3. Medical Examination - A fitness test as per the medical standards applicable to the specific post.
  4. Final Merit List - Prepared after successful completion of all the above stages.

RRB Group D Cut Off: 2022 vs 2018 Trends

Comparing past cycles helps candidates gauge how competitive the exam typically is, though each cycle's cut off depends on that year's specific vacancies and applicant numbers.

In the 2022 cycle, the CBT was conducted from 17 August to 11 October 2022, and cut off marks varied significantly by zone for instance, the UR normalised cut off ranged from around 60 to 70 marks depending on the region. In the 2018 cycle, cut off marks (on the older marking pattern) ranged roughly between 62 and 80 for the UR category across zones. Both cycles confirm that cut off marks fluctuate zone-to-zone based on vacancy count and competition level, a pattern that continues in 2026.

How to Download RRB NTPC Graduate CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026

Follow these simple steps to check your allotted exam city online.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective regional Railway Recruitment Board or use the direct link above.
  2. Locate the link labelled "CEN 06/2025 (NTPC Graduate): CBT-2 City Intimation."

  • Gate closing time
  • Candidate's photograph and signature
  • Exam-day instructions

How to Download RRB JE CBT 2 Hall Ticket 2026

The admit card download process is straightforward and uniform across all RRB zonal portals. Candidates should keep their Registration Number and Date of Birth ready before starting. Follow these steps to download the RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026 without any difficulty.

Step 1 - Go to the official RRB website rrbcdg.gov.in or directly visit rrb.digialm.com.

Candidates must take note of a special instruction issued by the Ministry of Railways regarding an additional requirement for the RRB JE CBT 2 2026 examination. This applies to all candidates appearing under CEN 05/2025.

As per the official notice, candidates are required to paste a recent colour photograph not older than six months on their admit card before entering the examination hall. While the original call letter mentioned that candidates should paste the same photograph submitted during the online application, the Railway Recruitment Board clarified that since a live photograph was already captured at the time of registration, a fresh recent colour photograph must now be affixed on the hall ticket. Failure to comply with this requirement may create issues at the exam centre.

RRB JE CBT 2 Exam Pattern 2026

The CBT 2 is a 150-mark computer-based test with a total duration of 120 minutes. The paper is divided into five sections, with the technical discipline section carrying the maximum weightage of 100 marks. There is a negative marking of one-third mark for every incorrect response. Candidates who have cleared CBT 1 should use the final days before 2 July 2026 to focus primarily on their engineering subject.

Documents to Carry on RRB JE Exam Day 2026

Carrying the correct set of documents is mandatory for entry into the examination hall. Candidates who do not bring the required ID proof along with their printed admit card may be denied entry, regardless of their registered status. Prepare all documents a day in advance to avoid any last-minute issues.

The mandatory documents to carry to the RRB JE CBT 2 Exam 2026 are:

  • Printed copy of RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026 (with recent photograph pasted)
  • Any one valid original Photo ID proof Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Driving Licence, or Passport
  • Two recent passport-size colour photographs
  • Aadhaar Card for biometric verification at the exam centre

Prohibited Items at RRB JE CBT 2 Exam Centre

Candidates are strictly prohibited from bringing certain items inside the examination hall. The Railway Recruitment Board enforces a zero-tolerance policy for possession of banned items. Any candidate found carrying restricted materials may be immediately disqualified and may face additional action.

Items not permitted inside the RRB JE exam hall:

  • Mobile phones and smartphones
  • Smartwatches and digital watches
  • Bluetooth devices and wireless earphones
  • Scientific or regular calculators
  • Books, notes, or printed study material of any kind
  • Writing instruments (pens and pencils) unless provided at the venue
  • Food items and water bottles
  • Handbags and pouches
  • Metallic jewellery and accessories

RRB JE Exam Day Guidelines 2026

Following all exam day instructions carefully helps candidates avoid unnecessary stress and ensures smooth entry and participation at the test centre. Read the guidelines below thoroughly before leaving for the exam.

  • Arrive at the examination centre at least 30 to 60 minutes before your assigned reporting time.
  • Carry the printed admit card along with a valid original photo ID and passport-size photographs.
  • Paste a recent colour photograph on the admit card before reaching the exam centre.
  • Do not bring any electronic devices, gadgets, or prohibited items to the venue.
  • Listen to all instructions provided by the invigilators inside the examination hall.
  • Maintain discipline at all times and avoid any form of unfair means or malpractice.
  • Ensure all required documents are gathered and verified the night before the exam.
  • Do not wait until the last day to download the admit card as heavy server traffic may cause delays.
